items.title: Libye : Washington presse les dirigeants de finaliser la transition et menace de sanctions

original_payload.original_title: Libye : Washington presse les dirigeants de finaliser la transition et menace de sanctions
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Libye : Washington presse les dirigeants de finaliser la transition et menace de sanctions
Les États-Unis ont exhorté les responsables libyens à accélérer la transition vers des élections, brandissant la menace de sanctions du Conseil de sécurité contre les obstacles potentiels.
Alwihda Info
16 oct. 2026
© DR
Les États-Unis ont exhorté, mercredi 14 octobre 2026, les responsables libyens à accélérer la mise en œuvre du processus politique devant conduire à des élections nationales, tout en avertissant que les personnes ou entités qui chercheraient à entraver cette transition pourraient faire l’objet de sanctions du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies.
S’exprimant lors d’une réunion du Conseil de sécurité consacrée à la situation en Libye, l’ambassadrice Jennifer Locetta, représentante alternative des États-Unis pour les affaires politiques spéciales, a salué l’accord conclu le 30 août à Tripoli, sous la facilitation de la Mission d’appui des Nations unies en Libye (MANUL). Selon Washington, cet accord doit permettre l’organisation d’élections nationales sous l’autorité d’un exécutif unifié.
La diplomate américaine a souligné que les États-Unis poursuivent parallèlement leurs efforts diplomatiques afin de soutenir les initiatives libyennes visant à réduire les divisions politiques et à unifier les institutions politiques, économiques et militaires du pays.
Elle a cité parmi les avancées récentes l’adoption du premier budget national unifié de la Libye depuis treize ans, ainsi que les exercices conjoints « Flintlock 2026 », qui ont réuni des forces de l’est et de l’ouest du pays sous la direction du Commandement des États-Unis pour l’Afrique (AFRICOM).
Washington estime que ses efforts sont complémentaires à la feuille de route de la MANUL, avec pour objectif commun la formation d’un exécutif unifié et l’organisation d’élections nationales reflétant la volonté du peuple libyen.
Jennifer Locetta a également appelé les parties libyennes à respecter et à mettre en œuvre l’accord dit « 4+4 ». Elle a salué la désignation d’une nouvelle direction à la Chambre des représentants, le 6 octobre, et encouragé le président Abdulnabi à coopérer avec la MANUL afin de finaliser rapidement les réformes électorales.
En revanche, les États-Unis se sont dits préoccupés par la position du Haut Conseil d’État, accusé par Washington de chercher à perturber le processus électoral en rejetant l’accord 4+4. La représentante américaine a rappelé que le Conseil de sécurité peut sanctionner les personnes ou organisations qui compromettent la transition politique ou la tenue des élections.
Inquiétudes autour des infrastructures énergétiques
Washington a également exprimé sa préoccupation face aux récentes attaques de drones contre des infrastructures énergétiques, qui ont provoqué des coupures d’électricité, des perturbations dans l’approvisionnement en eau ainsi que des manifestations à Tripoli, Zawiya et Misrata. La diplomate américaine a évoqué le blocage, en septembre, de l’oléoduc Sharara-Zawiya. Selon les chiffres cités par les États-Unis, cet incident aurait entraîné près de 95 millions de dollars de pertes de revenus pétroliers pour la Libye.
Les États-Unis appellent ainsi toutes les parties à faire preuve de retenue et à ne pas prendre pour cible les installations énergétiques, estimant qu’elles constituent des infrastructures essentielles pour l’ensemble de la population libyenne. Pour Washington, ces tensions démontrent que la situation actuelle ne peut perdurer et renforcent la nécessité de parvenir rapidement à un exécutif unifié ainsi qu’à un calendrier électoral crédible.
Les États-Unis ont enfin réaffirmé leur soutien au renouvellement du mandat de la MANUL et leur volonté de poursuivre leur coopération avec le Conseil de sécurité afin de soutenir une solution politique durable en Libye.

items.title: What’s the PHP coding flaw that could pull down 70 percent of the internet?

original_payload.original_title: What’s the PHP coding flaw that could pull down 70 percent of the internet?
original_payload.original_body:
Government websites in Europe and elsewhere have gone offline after news of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators scrambling to protect their systems.
Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday released urgent new fixes, saying all users were “encouraged to update immediately”.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Judge orders Meta to pay $25bn in fines for Facebook privacy violations
list 2 of 3  Meta faces Australian lawsuit over alleged social media harm to children
list 3 of 3  ‘Facebook’s wrongdoing’: Why has Meta been fined $25bn in New Mexico?
end of list
PHP runs on the servers that host websites, building pages behind the scenes before they reach a visitor’s browser. Most people never see it, but it powers everything from blogs to online shops and government portals.
The vulnerabilities, which had been lurking in the software for years, were uncovered with the help of artificial intelligence. Details about them leaked online on Tuesday before fixes were available, forcing PHP to rush them out.
Experts said they were bracing for a wave of intrusions as hackers jumped to get ahead of the updates.
What is the bug?
Andrew Cullen, a lecturer on AI and cybersecurity at the University of Melbourne, said many devices in the world are connected to one piece of foundational software, which is where the bug was found.
The vulnerability allows a hacker to run code on a website, meaning they could change the website or force it to release personal information collected in a database, Cullen told Al Jazeera.
Both flaws stem from how PHP handles fatal errors, such as running out of memory. Because the problem sits in PHP itself, even the simplest website running an affected version can be vulnerable, and attackers could read passwords and other credentials from a server’s memory, the cloud security company Wiz said. Both flaws scored 9.2 out of 10 on the industry’s standard severity scale, placing them in the “critical” category.

Sénégal : le Premier ministre accuse Pastef d'« obstruction » et la majorité riposte

Facebook  Twitter  WhatsApp
Le Premier ministre sénégalais  Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô  a accusé, dimanche 25 octobre 2026 à Dakar, les députés de Pastef de bloquer la loi de finances rectificative, deux jours avant la plénière.  « Il y a une différence entre l’obstruction du travail du Gouvernement et l’amendement. Poir rappel, la commission des Finances avait rejeté le texte vendredi, tout comme deux amendements de l’exécutif.
Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô  a invoqué l’article 82 de la Constitution, qui reconnaît aux députés le droit d’amender:  « Nous leur demandons de formuler les amendement…s Quand on fait de l’obstruction, on ne fait pas de l’ouverture » .
Il a toutefois adressé un message à  Ousmane Sonko,  président de l’Assemblée et de Pastef :  « Nous ne sommes pas des ennemis. Nous ne sommes pas des adversaires. L’exécutif et le législatif doivent dialoguer » .
Le parti a répliqué une heure plus tard, lors de son point de presse à la Résidence  Serigne Abass Sall.  La première réponse est venue du député  Amadou Ba  qui lui a demandé de  « se concentrer sur l’essentiel » , car la question  « ne le concerne pas » . Il lui a aussi demandé de cesser ses  « menaces »  et de rendre public tout dossier qu’il détiendrait contre Sonko.

original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : à Pala, la commune se dote d'équipements majeurs pour dynamiser ses services
La commune de Pala a reçu un important lot de matériels et d'équipements offert par le gouvernement pour renforcer ses services techniques et son administration municipale.
Alwihda Info
07 oct. 2026
Par Djonre Nentouing Ben-Casimir
La commune de Pala a considérablement renforcé ses capacités opérationnelles en réceptionnant un important lot de matériels et d'équipements. Cette dotation vise à optimiser le fonctionnement de l'administration municipale et à accroître l'efficacité des interventions sur le terrain.
La cérémonie officielle s'est déroulée mardi 6 octobre 2026 à l'hôtel de ville, en présence de nombreux responsables techniques et d'invités. Fourni par le gouvernement, cet appui logistique comprend deux véhicules pick-up de type Hilux, huit motos, six tricycles, un chargeur poids lourd, ainsi que des brouettes, du matériel d'hygiène et divers équipements de bureau.
Les clés des véhicules et les équipements ont été officiellement remises au maire de Pala, Dr Armi Jonas, par le préfet du département du Mayo-Dallah, Barka Abgoumsou, qui représentait pour l'occasion le Délégué général du Gouvernement auprès de la province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest.
Pour les services techniques de la municipalité, cet apport constitue un levier stratégique. Le directeur des services techniques, Koivoudou Lacatus, a souligné que ces équipements répondent directement aux urgences opérationnelles de la commune.
Lors de son allocution, le préfet Barka Abgoumsou a salué cette initiative gouvernementale, tout en exhortant les bénéficiaires et les responsables municipaux à faire un usage rigoureux et responsable de ce matériel.
De son côté, le maire Dr Armi Jonas s'est réjoui de ce renforcement des capacités d'action de la municipalité. Il a également appelé les différents services à veiller scrupuleusement à la préservation et à l'entretien de ces équipements.
Cette dotation permettra à la commune d'intensifier ses actions, notamment dans les secteurs des travaux publics, de l'hygiène et de l'assainissement, tout en améliorant durablement les conditions de travail des agents.

items.title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973

original_payload.original_title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973
original_payload.original_body:
Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Algeria recently donated four military helicopters to Niger (file photo)
By   Ondiro Oganga      and    Chris Ewokor   ,  BBC Africa
Published
26 October 2026, 13:18 GMT
Updated 3 hours ago
Algeria is to send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since sending forces to Egypt during the Arab-Israeli war in 1973.
The deployment follows a visit to Algiers by Niger's defence minister, as the country seeks support against armed groups, some of which are linked to al-Qaeda or Islamic State.
Algeria has economic interests in Niger, including a planned gas pipeline that would carry Nigerian gas through Niger to Algeria. The troops are expected to protect energy facilities in northern Niger, near the Libyan border.
The deployment comes as the two neighbours rebuild ties after a diplomatic rift in 2025, when Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers.
Algeria's upper house of parliament held an emergency session on Sunday to vote on the proposed deployment. According to AFP news agency, 148 of the 174 senators voted in favour. It was later backed by the lower house of parliament.
However, the timing and number of soldiers to be deployed have not been announced.
The move would mark the first use of a 2020 constitutional provision allowing overseas military deployments and a significant shift in Algeria's long-standing policy against sending forces abroad.
"We are not sending our soldiers to wage war in Niger, but for a mission to secure economic infrastructure," Algerian senator Belkacem Boulghiti told reporters after the vote.
Algeria's state-owned energy company, Sonatrach, has also signed an agreement with Niger's petroleum ministry to explore for oil in the Kafra region. Two exploration wells are estimated to contain 168 million and 100 million barrels, respectively, Reuters reported.
Relations between Algeria and Niger have not always been smooth in recent years.
Algeria condemned the 2023 coup that ousted Niger's elected President, Mohamed Bazoum, and brought Gen Abdourahamane Tchiani to power.
Tensions rose again in 2025 after Algeria shot down a Malian drone near its border. Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers in solidarity with Mali, a close ally which is also under military rule.
Relations have since improved. Tchiani visited Algeria in February 2026, and in late August, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune sent fighter jets to Niger to help suppress a coup attempt and also donated four military helicopters.

items.title: En Afrique du Sud, comment expliquer la prolifération d'armes à feu?

original_payload.original_title: En Afrique du Sud, comment expliquer la prolifération d'armes à feu?
original_payload.original_body:
Reportage Afrique
En Afrique du Sud, comment expliquer la prolifération d'armes à feu?
Publié le :  08/10/2026 - 00:00
Écouter - 02:08
L’Afrique du Sud, qui enregistre l’un des plus hauts taux d'homicides de la planète, avec environ 60 meurtres par jour, est aussi confrontée aux fusillades de masse. Deux fusillades sanglantes ont fait 28 morts en un seul week-end le 27 septembre. Parmi les nombreux facteurs qui expliquent cette situation : le nombre très important d’armes à feu illégales en circulation, lié, entre autres, au passé brutal du pays et de sa région, et à la corruption.
Un membre du Service de police sud-africain (SAPS) monte la garde derrière un cordon de police près d'un lieu de divertissement à Somerset West, le 27 septembre 2026, après qu'un groupe d'hommes armés a pris d'assaut les lieux.        © Gianluigi Guercia / AFP
Publicité
De notre correspondant à Johannesburg,
Beaucoup d’armes à feu illégales en Afrique du Sud viennent de pays voisins qui ont connu des conflits, comme le Mozambique, frappé par 15 ans de guerre civile. Certains stocks d’armes auraient ensuite été détournés par des réseaux criminels transnationaux. «  On estime qu'il y a 3,8 millions d'armes à feu illégales en circulation dans le pays,  souligne Jacob Mofokeng, professeur en criminologie à l’université de Pretoria.  En   Afrique du Sud  , la majorité des meurtres sont liés aux armes à feu. Et on le voit avec ces fusillades récentes qui ont fait 28 morts par balles en un seul week-end !  »
La nation arc-en-ciel a également hérité des armes de l’apartheid, un régime brutal et surarmé. Si aujourd’hui la police confisque des milliers d’armes à feu illégales chaque année, la corruption continue d’alimenter les réseaux criminels : «  Un colonel a été arrêté,  poursuit le criminologue , il travaillait au registre des armes à feu. Lorsque l'État confisquait certaines de ces armes, cet individu avait trouvé le moyen de les revendre aux membres de gangs.  »
À lire aussi  Afrique du Sud: deux fusillades à Johannesburg et au Cap font 27 morts
Remonter les réseaux criminels
Le gouvernement a mis en place   une commission d’enquête pour comprendre cette infiltration des réseaux criminels au sein de la police  . Cette commission, Stanley Maphosa, directeur de Gun Free Afrique du Sud, une organisation qui milite pour se débarrasser de la violence des armes à feu, la suit assidûment. «  Une seule arme peut être utilisée dans plusieurs fusillades. Le problème, c'est qu'en Afrique du Sud, on s’intéresse surtout au tireur, à celui qui appuie sur la gâchette,  explique-t-il.  Cette personne est recherchée puis arrêtée, mais on ne trace pas l’arme. D'où vient le réseau qui fournit ces AK-47 ? Comment pouvons-nous remonter jusqu'à ce réseau et parvenir à le démanteler ?  »
Pour afficher ce contenu Instagram, il est nécessaire d'autoriser les cookies de mesure d'audience et de publicité.
Accepter
Gérer mes choix
Selon lui, les communautés veulent aider, mais craignent les représailles : «  La majorité des gens ne veulent pas d'armes. Ils sont disposés à servir d'informateurs, mais ils ont peur, car les informateurs sont susceptibles d'être tués et ne bénéficient pas d'une protection suffisante , déplore Stanley Maphosa.  D'une certaine manière, cela crée un climat de peur et de normalisation. Je pense que la peur et la normalisation sont deux phénomènes bien présents dans les communautés.  »
Car l’Afrique du Sud enregistre en moyenne 60 homicides par jour. Et selon les autorités sud-africaines, les armes à feu restent le moyen le plus fréquemment utilisé pour commettre ces meurtres, devant les armes blanches.

items.title: Mode : la 15ᵉ édition de SAAMHA N’Djamena Fashion Week placée sous le thème « Le Tchad défile »

original_payload.original_title: Mode : la 15ᵉ édition de SAAMHA N’Djamena Fashion Week placée sous le thème « Le Tchad défile »
original_payload.original_body:
Lors d’une conférence de presse tenue ce 10 octobre, le comité d’organisation de SAAMHA N’Djamena Fashion Week a annoncé sa 15  ᵉ   édition. Placée sous le thème « Le Tchad défile », cette édition anniversaire mise sur les talents des dix arrondissements, la solidarité et l’entrepreneuriat culturel.
Lire aussi :  Mode : Saamha Fashion Week est à sa 12e édition
Créée en 2011 et portée par Mine De Rien, l’événement célèbre quinze ans de mode et de valorisation culturelle. Lors de la conférence de presse, sa promotrice Solkem Léonie Ngarmbatina a dévoilé les grandes lignes d’une manifestation consacrée à la créativité, aux savoir-faire locaux et aux échanges culturels africains. Depuis ses débuts, l’initiative ambitionne de « parler autrement du Tchad par la culture ».
L’innovation majeure de cette édition est la « Bataille des arrondissements ». Chaque commune de N’Djamena accueillera un spectacle associant défilés de mode et prestations artistiques, avec des participants issus de son territoire. Deux tenues seront retenues à chaque étape, soit vingt créations destinées à représenter les arrondissements lors du Grand Défilé. Les étapes sont prévues entre novembre et début décembre, à raison de deux arrondissements par semaine. La finale est annoncée pour le 10 décembre.
Lire aussi :  Mode : Saamha N’Djamena Fashion Week célèbre la mode africaine avec « Saamha In The Street »
SAAMHA XV réserve également une place à la responsabilité sociale avec le programme « SAAMHA for Kids ». Dans la continuité de l’action de 2025, les organisateurs prévoient de réhabiliter les toilettes d’une école et de contribuer à son approvisionnement en eau potable. Le volet économique prendra forme à travers des expositions-ventes du 11 au 13 décembre 2026, tandis que « SAAMHA Haute Couture » mettra l’accent sur les créations tchadiennes et africaines.

items.title: 25 civic educators trained to promote election awareness in Eastern Equatoria

original_payload.original_title: 25 civic educators trained to promote election awareness in Eastern Equatoria
original_payload.original_body:
The Support Peace Initiative Development Organization (SPIDO), a civil society group, has trained 25 civic educators in South Sudan’s Eastern Equatoria state to raise public awareness of electoral processes ahead of planned elections in December 2026.
The training, held in Torit on Wednesday with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), covered democracy, human rights, inclusion, governance and voting procedures.
SPIDO programme officer Advocate Morris John Peter said the participants would return to their communities to share the knowledge gained during the training.
“We need to equip them with the basic knowledge and principles of democracy and electoral processes so that they understand what is happening and the different stages of the election process,” he said.
The participants represented local government institutions, civil society organisations, women’s and youth groups, organisations representing people with disabilities, academic institutions, security forces and the electoral commission.
Peter said security personnel were included because of their role in protecting the electoral process and their right to participate in elections as citizens.
Noma Samuel, one of the participants, said the training had improved her understanding of her rights and responsibilities as a South Sudanese citizen.
She urged civil society organisations to extend civic education to remote communities, saying an emphasis on urban areas could leave rural residents without adequate information about the electoral process.
Another participant, Ebul Simon Ohuro, called on the government and development partners to provide resources to expand civic education across Eastern Equatoria, including translating information into local languages and making it accessible to vulnerable groups.
Ohuro said rural communities need clear information about voter registration and voting procedures to help eligible citizens make informed decisions and participate in the elections.
South Sudan is scheduled to hold elections in December 2026. The country has faced prolonged political and security challenges since gaining independence in 2011, raising concerns about the conditions for holding a credible vote.
The extent to which civic education reaches rural communities will be important in ensuring that voters have access to information about electoral procedures before polling day.

items.title: Italy approves sweeping security measures in response to protests

original_payload.original_title: Italy approves sweeping security measures in response to protests
original_payload.original_body:
Italy has approved the deployment of troops and tougher legal penalties in a bid to quell cost-of-living protests in the north of the country that occasionally turned violent over the weekend.
The Italian cabinet on Tuesday approved sending 500 troops to Milan, a new legal offence covering violent participation in a demonstration, tougher penalties for rioters and financial liability for parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.

list 2 of 3  France’s growing debt woes: How bond markets set countries’ borrowing costs
list 3 of 3  Portugal cost-of-living protesters pour back into camps cleared by police
end of list
Italy’s Ministry of Defence said the military will help reinforce security at key sites, step up surveillance of sensitive locations and enhance monitoring.
Unrest swept northern Italian cities at the weekend, including the financial capital Milan, where groups of mainly young people looted shops, smashed windows and clashed with the police. The demonstrations were driven by anger over soaring fuel and energy prices, high rents, low wages and the state of public services.
Public safety
As part of the new legal measures, which take effect immediately, anyone who takes part in a group of at least five people and endangers public safety during protests faces up to five years in prison and a maximum fine of €20,000 ($22,460).
Penalties increase if faces are concealed or people are injured.
Authorities can order prompt compensation for any damage inflicted and, in the case of minors, hold their parents liable.
Police will be allowed to detain youths aged between 14 and 17, even if they have not committed a crime, provided there is evidence they pose a danger, extending powers that previously applied only to adults.

items.title: NGIJ urges FG to immortalise Dele Giwa

original_payload.original_title: NGIJ urges FG to immortalise Dele Giwa
original_payload.original_body:
General News  NGIJ urges FG to immortalise Dele Giwa
By  Wandoo Sombo   ·   27 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
​‌⁠‍By Ebere Agozie
The Nigerian Guild of Investigative Journalists (NGIJ) has urged the Federal Government to immortalise the late Dele Giwa, in recognition of his contributions to democratic accountability and the public’s right to information. .
This is contained in a a statement issued by NGIJ President, Malam Abdulrahman Aliagan and Secretary, Rowland Olonishuwa.
The guild described Giwa as a symbol of journalistic courage whose commitment to fearless reporting helped shape investigative journalism in Nigeria.
“The federal government should consider naming a public institution, national journalism centre, media research facility or another appropriate national monument after the late journalist.
“Such recognition would affirm the vital role of journalists in nation-building and inspire younger generations to embrace courage, integrity and service to the public interest.
“National recognition should extend beyond political leaders and public officeholders to include professionals whose sacrifices have significantly advanced democratic development and the protection of citizens’ rights.
The guild also demanded for justice for the slained investigative journalist, said four decades without accountability must not become a symbol of impunity.
It noted that Giwa’s legacy transcends his professional achievements, embodying journalism’s responsibility to question authority, expose wrongdoing, defend the public interest and hold those in power accountable.
“Forty years after Dele Giwa was murdered, Nigeria must not allow his sacrifice to fade into history.
“His life represented the courage to investigate the powerful and defend the public’s right to know.
“His death remains a painful reminder of the price journalists can pay for pursuing the truth,” NGIJ stated.
As part of efforts to preserve Giwa’s legacy and strengthen investigative journalism, NGIJ announced plans to establish the Dele Giwa Annual Public Lecture on Investigative Journalism, which will be the Guild’s maiden public lecture.
It said the initiative will provide a platform for journalists, media executives, policymakers, academics, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to discuss press freedom, investigative reporting, democratic accountability and the safety of journalists.
“Beyond commemorating Giwa, the annual lecture will promote professional independence, courage, accuracy and ethical responsibility while exploring practical solutions to the challenges confronting investigative journalism in Nigeria.
“We do not want Dele Giwa to be remembered only through anniversary tributes. We want his name to become a permanent institution in advancing investigative journalism in Nigeria,” the guild declared.
The guild expressed concern that the circumstances surrounding his assassination remained unresolved four decades later.
It called on the federal government, law enforcement agencies and relevant judicial authorities to renew efforts to establish the circumstances of his death, review available evidence and pursue credible investigative leads in accordance with the law.
It reiterated that the passage of time must not extinguish the quest for justice or diminish the state’s responsibility to investigate the killing of a Nigerian citizen and distinguished journalist.
“A nation cannot adequately honour a journalist who died in the pursuit of truth while allowing the questions surrounding his murder to remain unanswered.
“Remembrance must be accompanied by action, and tributes must translate into a renewed commitment to justice, accountability and the protection of journalists.
Nigerian journalists, particularly young and aspiring investigative reporters, the guild said should draw inspiration from Giwa’s courage while upholding the highest standards of accuracy, fairness, verification, independence and ethical conduct.
The guild reaffirmed its commitment to promoting credible, independent and impact-driven investigative journalism through professional training, institutional partnerships, public-interest investigations and accountability initiatives.
It also called on media organisations, government institutions, civil society groups, development partners and the public to support efforts to improve journalists’ safety, strengthen newsroom independence and create an enabling environment for responsible reporting.
It urged the federal fovernment and the media industry to ensure that Giwa’s legacy is remembered not only for the tragedy of his unresolved assassination but also for his enduring contribution to the pursuit of truth.
“Dele Giwa may have been silenced 40 years ago, but the ideals he represented must never be silenced.
“His legacy must live on in every journalist who dares to investigate, every report that exposes wrongdoing, every institution held accountable and every citizen empowered by the truth,” NGIJ concluded.
Giwa, co-founder and pioneer Editor-in-Chief of Newswatch magazine, was killed by a parcel bomb delivered to his Lagos residence on Oct. 19, 1986, during the military era.
Forty years after the incident, his assassination remained unresolved, with no one held accountable for the murder. (NAN)
Edited by Sadiya Hamza

items.title: Ex-NCAA Staff Member Accuses Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo Of Blocking Reinstatement Despite Court Judgment

original_payload.original_title: Ex-NCAA Staff Member Accuses Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo Of Blocking Reinstatement Despite Court Judgment
original_payload.original_body:
A former Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) employee, Annastasia Nneka Anukwa, has accused the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, of frustrating her reinstatement despite a court judgment nullifying her dismissal and ordering the agency to restore her employment.
Anukwa, who joined the NCAA in July 2001 and rose to Assistant Chief Accountant, Grade Level 13, Step 08, told SaharaReporters that she remains out of work despite a favourable judgment delivered by the National Industrial Court in Uyo on December 13, 2024.
She alleges that Keyamo, whose law firm previously handled her case, failed to help secure compliance with the judgment after becoming minister and subsequently intervened in ways she believes prolonged the dispute.
The allegations are contained in a petition dated October 23, 2026, addressed to the Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court and Secretary of the Legal Practitioners Privileges Committee (LPPC), in which Anukwa called for a fuller investigation into her case and the conduct of the lawyers who represented her.
Anukwa Says Keyamo's Chambers Handled Her Case
Anukwa said she approached Keyamo's chambers for legal assistance around 2015, claiming she was unaware at the time that he was acting as a lawyer for the aviation ministry.
She alleged that Keyamo personally reviewed her case, agreed that it had merit and assigned lawyers from his chambers to represent her.
In her petition, she wrote that Keyamo “was the one I personally approached, he reviewed my case and assigned me the lawyers that represented me.”
She added that she regularly updated him on the proceedings.
“Also I always give Mr Festus Keyamo updates on my matter. Therefore, he has been in the know of all that transpired,” she wrote.
Anukwa alleged that the case dragged on for about four years without a hearing before she withdrew it in 2019 and engaged another law firm.
She questioned why Keyamo's chambers accepted the case despite what she described as the firm's connection to the aviation ministry at the time.

items.title: Nobel d’économie 2026 : quand l’avenir guide les banques centrales

original_payload.original_title: Nobel d’économie 2026 : quand l’avenir guide les banques centrales
original_payload.original_body:
Une banque centrale peut-elle maîtriser l’inflation sans comprendre ce que les ménages et les entreprises anticipent ? Robert E. Hall et Michael Woodford, récompensés le 12 octobre 2026 par le prix de la Banque de Suède en sciences économiques en mémoire d’Alfred Nobel, ont montré que non : pour stabiliser l’économie, il faut comprendre les comportements qui produisent les chiffres.
Quand les anciens modèles ont vacillé
L’idée de stabiliser l’économie remonte à John Maynard Keynes : la demande ne s’aligne pas d’elle-même sur ce que l’économie peut produire. Les gouvernements soutiennent alors la demande par la dépense publique, les banques centrales ajustent leurs taux d’intérêt.
Les crises pétrolières des années 1970 ont mis ces modèles à l’épreuve. L’inflation et le chômage ont augmenté ensemble, contredisant les relations statistiques sur lesquelles reposaient les politiques économiques. Robert Lucas, Nobel 1995, en a tiré la leçon : les modèles doivent partir des décisions individuelles des ménages et des entreprises, qui, additionnées, façonnent l’économie entière.
Hall et Woodford, deux contributions complémentaires
En 1978, Robert Hall part d’une hypothèse : les ménages règlent leurs dépenses sur les revenus qu’ils attendent à long terme. Une hausse de salaire déjà prévue est donc intégrée d’avance ; seule une information nouvelle fait varier leur consommation. Le test lui donne raison. En 1982, avec Frederic Mishkin, il estime qu’environ 80 % des ménages se comportent ainsi, les autres vivant au jour le jour.
Michael Woodford assemble les pièces. Dans  Interest and Prices , publié en 2003, il propose un modèle en trois équations : la consommation, l’inflation et la règle de la banque centrale. Inspiré du Suédois Knut Wicksell et de son taux d’intérêt « naturel », il montre qu’une banque centrale peut piloter l’économie par les taux plutôt que par la quantité de monnaie.
Source: Amazon livre
Pourquoi sa crédibilité est-elle si importante ? Parce que les entreprises et les ménages décident aujourd’hui en fonction de ce qu’ils pensent qu’il se passera demain. Si une banque centrale convainc qu’elle empêchera l’inflation de s’installer, elle influence leurs comportements dès maintenant. Ces modèles servent désormais aux banques centrales et aux ministères des Finances du monde entier.
Un outil, pas une recette universelle
Ces modèles ne suppriment ni les crises ni les arbitrages. Face à une flambée des prix de l’énergie, ils recommandent, contrairement aux anciens, de relever les taux pour éviter que l’inflation ne s’installe. Mais une hausse des taux ralentit aussi l’activité : la banque centrale doit apprécier la durée du choc et le risque de propagation aux salaires et aux prix.
La question est plus aiguë pour les économies dépendantes des matières premières. Au Tchad, c’est la BEAC qui fixe un taux unique pour les six pays de la CEMAC, avec un franc CFA arrimé à l’euro. Et une hausse des taux ne crée ni électricité, ni devises, ni capacités de production. Les contraintes structurelles limitent ce que la politique monétaire peut accomplir seule.
Reste à savoir jusqu’où des modèles nés dans des économies diversifiées éclairent celles qui vivent du pétrole.
GADNODJI Nako
Sources : Académie royale des sciences de Suède, communiqué et documents scientifiques du 12 octobre 2026.

Ahead of Monday’s official gala, here’s everything to know about the award, its history and more:
What is the Ballon d’Or?
The Ballon d’Or is the highest individual award given to a footballer, based on his or her performance in the previous season.
The award was created in 1956 by two sports writers, Gabriel Hanot and Jacques Ferran, from France Football, a French magazine.
Originally, the men’s award was limited to European players, but in 1995 it was expanded to include all players of any origin active at European clubs. Finally, in 2007, it became a global award with all professional footballers being eligible.
The women’s Ballon d’Or started in 2018 when Ada Hegerberg was named the inaugural winner.
The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) and Groupe Amaury – owners of France Football and L’Equipe – have co-organised the Ballon d’Or since the 2024 edition.
Who decides the Ballon d’Or winner?
The winner is chosen by an international jury of specialised journalists, with one representative per country: the top 100 nations according to the FIFA rankings for the men’s award, and the top 50 for the women’s award.

items.title: Moyen-Chari : les médiateurs agropastoraux renforcent leur collaboration

original_payload.original_title: Moyen-Chari : les médiateurs agropastoraux renforcent leur collaboration
original_payload.original_body:
Le Centre pour le Dialogue Humanitaire (HD) a réuni, du 2 au 3 octobre 2026 à Sarh, les acteurs engagés dans la prévention des conflits entre agriculteurs et éleveurs. La rencontre vise à renforcer le dialogue et la collaboration entre les différents réseaux de médiateurs agropastoraux du Moyen-Chari.
La rencontre a rassemblé notamment des sous-préfets, des chefs traditionnels ainsi que des médiateurs agropastoraux venus de plusieurs localités de la province. Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « Prévention et atténuation de l’impact des conflits locaux dans les zones frontalières d’Afrique centrale ».
Pour le chargé de médiation du Centre pour le Dialogue Humanitaire, Nadji Nelambaye, cette rencontre offre une occasion aux différents acteurs de partager leurs expériences et de réfléchir ensemble aux difficultés rencontrées sur le terrain.
Selon lui, plusieurs situations peuvent alimenter les tensions entre communautés, notamment l’accès aux terres agricoles, aux pâturages et aux points d’eau, mais aussi la transhumance, la divagation des animaux et les difficultés liées aux couloirs de passage.
Dans ce contexte, il estime que les médiateurs occupent une place importante. « Présents au plus près des communautés, ils peuvent intervenir rapidement pour favoriser le dialogue, rapprocher les parties en conflit et contribuer à trouver des solutions acceptées par les différents protagonistes », a-t-il précisé.
Nadji Nelambaye insiste également sur les principes qui doivent guider leur travail : l’écoute, la neutralité, l’impartialité et le respect entre les parties. « Notre responsabilité est grande, mais notre engagement collectif peut faire la différence », a-t-il déclaré.
Lire aussi  :  Logone occidental : les membres des réseaux des médiateurs agropastoraux outillés en techniques de gestion des enjeux fonciers et des ressources naturelles
Présent à la rencontre, le secrétaire général du département du Barh-Koh, Ngomsembaye Allahoguina Voltaire, a salué l’initiative du Centre pour le Dialogue Humanitaire. Il a rappelé que les questions de paix et de sécurité dépassent les frontières et que le Tchad reste exposé aux effets des crises qui touchent certains pays voisins.
Pour lui, ces situations peuvent avoir des conséquences directes sur les communautés vivant dans les zones rurales, aussi bien du côté des agriculteurs que des éleveurs.
Le secrétaire général a par ailleurs appelé les médiateurs à préserver la confiance placée en eux par les populations et les autorités. Il a insisté sur la nécessité pour ces acteurs de rester impartiaux et neutres dans leurs interventions. Il a assuré que les autorités administratives et traditionnelles continueront à les accompagner dans leurs missions.
Les réseaux de Maro, Sido, Djek-Djeke, Moussoro, Danamadji-Moyo, Djoli-Balimba et Komogo-Sandana ont pris part à cette rencontre inter-réseaux.

items.title: Rwanda: What Rwanda's New Central Bank Law Really Changes

original_payload.original_title: Rwanda: What Rwanda's New Central Bank Law Really Changes
original_payload.original_body:
On 24 July 2026, Rwanda published Law No. 033/2026 of 24/07/2026 governing the National Bank of Rwanda (the 2026 Law). Most commentary focuses on what the law says today. I find it more useful to ask where it comes from, as it is the latest milestone on a journey that began in 1964, two years after Rwanda's first Constitution. Since then, the central bank's legal framework and the Constitution have continued to evolve side by side.
The 1964 law created the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) as an autonomous public institution with capital of Rwf30 million. Its mission was to keep the currency stable and steer credit and foreign exchange towards the country's economic development. It operated under a three-member Board comprising the Governor and two administrators. The State could owe the bank up to half of the previous year's revenue. The bank was autonomous on paper, but it served as the government's banker and lender.

items.title: Nigeria seeks trade, economic cooperation in Pan-African diplomacy

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria seeks trade, economic cooperation in Pan-African diplomacy
original_payload.original_body:
Foreign  Nigeria seeks trade, economic cooperation in Pan-African diplomacy
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   3 hours ago   ·  6 min read
✓
✓
By Joshua Olomu
The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Amb. Sola Enikanolaiye, has urged African governments to place trade and economic cooperation at the centre of Pan-African diplomacy.
He made the call in his speech at a ministerial roundtable on “Trade and Economic Cooperation at the Centre of Pan-african Diplomacy” on Friday in Egypt.
The roundtable was hosted by Dr Badr Abdelatty, Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates of the Arab Republic of Egypt.
It was attended by ministers of states, representatives of the African Union Commission, AUDA-NEPAD, the AfCFTA Secretariat, Afreximbank and the Regional Economic Communities, amongst other stakeholders.
According to the minister, the theme of the roundtable speaks directly to how African countries should conduct their diplomacy in this decade.
“For too long, we treated trade and diplomacy as separate tracks, with foreign ministries managing relationships and trade ministries managing transactions.
“Experience has taught us otherwise,” he said.
The minister said partnerships endure only when they rest on shared economic interests, anchored on the wellbeing  of citizens.
He added that economic ambitions are realised only in an environment of trust, predictability and common purpose.
“That is why Nigeria welcomes a conversation that places trade and economic cooperation at the centre of Pan-African diplomacy.
“For Nigeria, Africa is the centrepiece of our foreign policy. We are the continent’s most populous nation, with a young and enterprising population of well over two hundred million people.
“Our stake in an integrated continent is therefore concrete. A larger, better-connected African market is an opportunity for our manufacturers, farmers, innovators and service providers, and equally for theirs,” he said.
Enikanolaiye said Nigeria was championing initiatives that promote trade and economic cooperation across the continent.
According to him, the digital economy offers, perhaps, the fastest route to a truly continental market.
“Young Nigerian innovators are building payment, logistics and financial services platforms that serve customers well beyond our borders.
“In the second quarter of this year, the information and communication sector grew by 9.62 per cent, more than twice the pace of the economy as a whole,” he said.
He added that the sector also contributed 11.74 per cent of real GDP, with about 156.9 million internet users recorded.
According to the minister, Nigeria ratified the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol in Nov. 2025 and is a co-champion of the Protocol, together with Kenya and South Africa.
“We are ready to share that experience and to learn from the experience of others,”he said.
The minister said Nigeria was  also supporting African capital with initiatives such as the Economic Development Tax Incentive
He said the incentive, administered by the Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission, has offered qualifying investors in priority sectors a tax credit of 5 per cent a year for five years on eligible capital expenditure.
“The Commission’s One-Stop Investment Centre brings together twenty-seven government agencies to help investors navigate approvals.
“We believe that the most durable investments on this continent will be those that African businesses make in one another.
In this regard, Aliko Dangote of Nigeria is setting the pace across Africa, to the applause and admiration of all,” he said.
At the sub-regional level, Enikanolaiye said ECOWAS has already laid the foundation through its Trade Liberalisation Scheme.
“The African Continental Free Trade Area is the most important trade instrument we have built together. As of September, fifty Pan -African of the fifty-four signatory countries have deposited their instruments of ratification.
“The Guided Trade Initiative has grown from seven participating countries to thirty-nine,” he said.
According to him, Nigeria validated its National AfCFTA Implementation Strategy, gazetted its Provisional Schedule of Tariff Concessions for trade in goods in April 2025.
He said the country also submitted its schedule of specific commitments on services through ECOWAS in Oct. 2025, and ratified the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol in Nov. 2025.
“We have also begun trading under the Guided Trade Initiative.
“A dedicated air cargo corridor linking Nigeria to East and Southern Africa, developed with Uganda Airlines and the United Nations Development Programme, has reportedly cut freight costs for participating businesses by between 50 and 75 per cent.
“Yet an agreement on paper does not move goods. The task before us now is to make it work at the border, at the port and at the bank,” he said.
According to the minister, trade cannot flow without finance, noting that African exporters still pay too much for credit, and too much of trades are  still settled in third currencies.
“Institutions such as Afreximbank, whose headquarters is in Cairo, and platforms such as the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System show what becomes possible when Africans build financial infrastructure for African needs.
“In April 2025, the Central Bank of Nigeria directed all banks to adopt PAPSS and begin originating transactions on the platform,” he said.
He said the CBN initiative has simplified documentation for PAPSS payments, allowing individuals to transact up to 2,000 United States dollars and companies up to 5,000 dollars on the strength of their existing customer documentation.
“It also allowed authorised dealer banks to source foreign exchange for PAPSS settlements through the official market. These payments can be made in local currencies, which reduces reliance on third currencies,” he said.
The minister identified slow and costly border procedures, underdeveloped logistics corridors as some non-tariff barriers   facing  trade across the continent.
“Movement of business people is still too restricted. And too much of our raw material leaves the continent without being processed.
“These are problems that no trade ministry can solve alone. They call for the kind of sustained political engagement that only diplomacy can provide,” he said.
Moving forward, Enikanolaiye urged that trade facilitation become a standing item in Pan-African diplomatic engagement, with regular coordination among our foreign, trade and finance ministries.
According to him, there is need for states to act decisively on non-tariff barriers, simplify border procedures and move towards the mutual recognition of standards.
He also called for widening of access to trade finance and local-currency settlement, particularly for small businesses, women traders and young entrepreneurs.
“Fourth, we should invest jointly in transport and energy corridors and in regional value chains, so that more of what Africa produces is processed in Africa.
“Fifth, we should speak with one voice in all multilateral external trade and investment negotiations, because our bargaining position is stronger when we stand together,” he said.
While commending the strong bilateral ties between Nigeria and Egypt, Enikanolaiye noted that both countries were two of Africa’s largest economies and long-standing partners in the cause of continental renewal.
“Our two countries held a Nigeria-Egypt Business Forum in Abuja in July 2025, where Nigeria proposed a Nigeria-Egypt Joint Investment Council.
“On   the sidelines of the Eighth Ministerial Meeting of the AfCFTA in Abuja this year, Egypt and Nigeria agreed to hold technical meetings on joint projects in digital identity and digital transformation.
“We look forward to working with Egypt to ensure that these fresh initiatives are implemented,” he said.

Nobel Prize
The Nobel Prize in medicine has been awarded to three scientists whose work explains how the brain switches individual nerve cells on and off.
The winners are Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel. Their research focuses on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, techniques that allow scientists to control and study nerve cells using light. Deisseroth is based in the United States, while Hegemann and Nagel work in Germany.
The Nobel committee praised the breakthrough, saying the method is now being used in laboratories around the world to reveal the brain’s mysteries.

“Effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption,” added the leader of the Catholic Church.
The American Pope’s comments come days after US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said on Thursday that the firing squad execution of  Nidal Malik Hasan  on December 3 will be livestreamed.
Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others in a shooting at the Fort Hood military base in 2009.
Pope Leo did not specifically refer to the planned execution, or last month’s botched execution attempt on  Christa Pike , who survived two doses of the lethal injection in Tennessee.
But his post came hours after his top deputy, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, told Vatican News that the plan to livestream Hasan’s execution was “unacceptable”.
It was Leo’s predecessor, Pope Francis, in 2018 who first amended official Catholic teaching to declare capital punishment “inadmissible” in all circumstances.

items.title: Tchad : à Sarh, la rectrice de l'Académie du Sud-Est à l'écoute des établissements de formation

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : à Sarh, la rectrice de l'Académie du Sud-Est à l'écoute des établissements de formation
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : à Sarh, la rectrice de l'Académie du Sud-Est à l'écoute des établissements de formation
En visite à Sarh, la rectrice de l'Académie du Sud-Est, le professeur Khadija Hassaballah Hamid, a recueilli les doléances des responsables d'établissements pour améliorer la formation des jeunes.
Alwihda Info
16 oct. 2026
Par Elwood Dk
La Rectrice de l'Académie du Sud-Est, le professeur Khadija Hassaballah Hamid, a poursuivi, le jeudi 15 octobre 2026, sa tournée dans les établissements d'enseignement et de formation de Sarh. Accompagnée de son équipe technique, elle s'est rendue au Centre de formation technique et professionnelle de Sarh ainsi qu'à l'Université Saint Charles Lwanga, avec pour objectif de s'informer sur leurs conditions de fonctionnement, d'identifier les difficultés rencontrées et de recueillir les propositions des responsables pour améliorer la formation des jeunes Tchadiens.
Au Centre de formation technique et professionnelle, la délégation a échangé avec le professeur Djimoko Bongo, responsable de l'ENSET. Après avoir présenté le fonctionnement de sa structure, celui-ci a exposé les difficultés financières qui complçoivent la réalisation de certaines activités.
La mission a également rencontré Adoumbaye Guidéyanan Djiadingué, responsable du nouveau Centre de formation technique et professionnelle de Sarh. Les discussions ont principalement porté sur le recrutement des apprenants et l'entretien des infrastructures de ce nouvel établissement, appelé à contribuer à la formation professionnelle des jeunes. Le responsable a également présenté plusieurs préoccupations liées au fonctionnement du centre. La prise en compte de ces besoins apparaît essentielle pour assurer la durabilité des installations et offrir aux apprenants un cadre d'apprentissage adapté.
La délégation s'est ensuite rendue à l'Université Saint Charles Lwanga de Sarh. À cette occasion, le recteur, le professeur Toḯngar Mogota Anatole, a présenté son institution et les principales difficultés auxquelles elle fait face. Parmi les préoccupations soulevées figurent les problèmes de déplacement des étudiants ainsi que l'insuffisance du personnel enseignant dans certaines filières, notamment les mathématiques et l'informatique. « Nous rencontrons des difficultés liées au déplacement des étudiants. Nous faisons également face à un manque d'enseignants dans certaines filières, particulièrement en mathématiques et en informatique », a-t-il expliqué.
Ces défis menacent la continuité des enseignements et la qualité des conditions offertes aux étudiants.
Au terme de ces rencontres, la Rectrice de l'Académie du Sud-Est a salué les efforts fournis par les équipes en faveur de la jeunesse tchadienne. Elle a pris note des doléances et s'est engagée à les transmettre aux autorités compétentes pour l'élaboration de solutions adaptées. « Cette tournée nous permet de mieux comprendre les réalités des établissements d'enseignement supérieur et de formation professionnelle de Sarh. Nous devons remonter leurs besoins auprès des autorités, dans l'intérêt de la qualité de l'enseignement et de la formation de nos étudiants », a-t-elle conclu.

items.title: Mauritanie: reconduit dans ses fonctions, le Premier ministre Moctar Ould Diay nomme un nouveau gouvernement

original_payload.original_title: Mauritanie: reconduit dans ses fonctions, le Premier ministre Moctar Ould Diay nomme un nouveau gouvernement
original_payload.original_body:
Mauritanie: reconduit dans ses fonctions, le Premier ministre Moctar Ould Diay nomme un nouveau gouvernement
La composition du nouveau gouvernement mauritanien a été révélée dans la soirée du samedi 10 octobre. Reconduit dans ses fonctions la veille par le chef de l'État, le Premier ministre sortant Moctar Ould Diay a constitué une équipe composée de 29 ministres. Mis en cause dans les incendies des deux centrales électriques de la Somelec survenus à la fin du mois d'août à Nouakchott, le ministre sortant de l'Énergie, Mohamed Ould Khaled, n'en fait pas partie.
Publié le :  11/10/2026 - 05:01
2 min     Temps de lecture
Le palais présidentiel à Nouakchott, en Mauritanie. Vendredi 9 octobre, le président mauritanien a reconduit le Premier ministre sortant Moctar Ould Diay, démissionnaire, dans ses fonctions.         © Ivik93, CC BY-SA 4.0
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Avec notre correspondant à Nouakchott,   Moussa Oumar Barry
En   Mauritanie  , la composition du nouveau gouvernement a été dévoilée tard dans la soirée du samedi 10 octobre, 24 heures après que le président a reconduit dans ses fonctions le Premier ministre sortant, Moctar Ould Diay, qui lui avait remis la démission de son équipe à la suite de la publication du rapport sur les incendies des deux centrales électriques de la Somelec survenus les 21 et 22 août derniers.
À lire aussi  Mauritanie: le Premier ministre sortant reconduit dans ses fonctions après avoir remis la démission de son gouvernement
Rapportant des dysfonctionnements, des défaillances au niveau des responsabilités, ainsi que l'usage de documents falsifiés, le document mettait notamment en cause l'ex-ministre de l'Énergie, Mohamed Ould Khaled, ainsi que plusieurs hauts responsables du secteur énergétique, dans cette affaire. Les incendies avaient, dans la foulée, provoqué d'importantes coupures d'électricité dans la capitale.
Huit femmes
Rajeuni, le nouveau gouvernement passe de 25 à 29 ministres. Et sans surprise, Mohamed Ould Khaled en a été évincé. En poste depuis 2024, celui-ci est remplacé par Mohamed Ould Abdel Fattah, qui avait déjà hérité de ce portefeuille dans le passé.
Reste que l'ancien ministre de l'Énergie n'est pas le seul à faire les frais de ce remaniement : des 25 ministres de l'ancien gouvernement, 12 n'ont pas été intégré à la nouvelle équipe - et six ont changé de ministère. Les départs les plus notables sont ceux de Mohamed Ahmed Ould Mohamed Lemine, à l'Intérieur, et de Hanena Ould Sidi, à la Défense, respectivement remplacés par Moctar Ahmed Bousseif et Ba Ousmane.
Enfin, huit femmes font partie du nouveau cabinet. Parmi elles figurent notamment Ba Aïssata Yahya, qui a été désignée secrétaire générale à la Présidence, et Aïssata Lam, qui hérite du ministère de la Pêche. Cette dernière entre en fonctions au moment où la Mauritanie et l'Union européenne renégocient l'accord de pêche qui les lie et qui prend fin au mois de novembre.

items.title: Bénin: la Police clarifie les circonstances de l'accident de Zogbodomey

original_payload.original_title: Bénin: la Police clarifie les circonstances de l'accident de Zogbodomey
original_payload.original_body:
Eric Orou Yérima, porte-parole de la Police Républicaine. Photo : DR
Bénin: la Police clarifie les circonstances de l'accident de Zogbodomey
20/10/2026    par    Armel TOGNON
Facebook  Twitter  WhatsApp
La police républicaine a profité d’un communiqué publié sur sa page Facebook ce lundi 19 octobre pour se prononcer sur l’accident qui s’est produit au cours du week-end écoulé à Zogboodomey. L’institution a apporté des clarifications sur les circonstances de ce drame et a tenu rétablir la vérité des chiffres face aux informations qui circulent sur les réseaux sociaux aainsi que dans certains médias. On retiendra donc du communiqué qu’il s’agit d’un camion chargé de briques s’est renversé dimanche 18 octobre 2026 sur la route nationale inter-États n°2 (RNIE 2), à hauteur de Hlagba-Zakpo, dans l’arrondissement de Massi, commune de Zogbodomey.
Un mort et quatre blessés, dont un grièvement atteint. C’est le bilan provisoire communiqué par la police. L’accident s’est produit aux environs de 16 heures. Alors que le conducteur abordait une descente, le camion aurait perdu son équilibre avant de se renverser sur la chaussée. Le poids lourd a ainsi bloqué la circulation dans les deux sens.
(📲 Rejoignez dès maintenant  👉     la communauté de La Nouvelle Tribune sur WhatsApp  !)
La circulation rétablie après quatre heures
Alertée, la Police républicaine s’est rendue sur les lieux pour effectuer les constatations nécessaires et organiser la circulation. Une grue a été mobilisée pour dégager le camion accidenté. Le trafic a finalement repris aux environs de 20 heures, soit quatre heures après le drame.
Face aux informations relayées sur les réseaux sociaux et dans certains médias, faisant état de nombreuses pertes en vies humaines, la Police républicaine a tenu à préciser le bilan provisoire. Elle a également exprimé sa compassion à la famille de la personne décédée et souhaité un prompt rétablissement aux blessés. Une enquête a été ouverte pour déterminer les causes exactes de l’accident et établir les responsabilités éventuelles. À ce stade, les circonstances précises du renversement restent donc à élucider.

items.title: Estate planning key to preventing inheritance disputes — legal practitioner

original_payload.original_title: Estate planning key to preventing inheritance disputes — legal practitioner
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Estate planning key to preventing inheritance disputes — legal practitioner
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   1 hour ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌‍‌‌​‍⁠⁠‌⁠⁠‍⁠‍‍‍⁠‌​ By Oluwatope Lawanson
A legal practitioner, Mr Olumide Olaiya, has advised Nigerians to write their wills as a practical step to prevent future family disputes.
Olaiya, Co-Founder of Castle eWill & Trust, said estate planning offers families clarity, prevents disputes, and urged Nigerians not to leave loved ones guessing their intentions.
He spoke on Thursday at the unveiling of Castle eWill & Trust, a digital platform designed to make will writing and trust creation more accessible and convenient.
He said the initiative was driven by the need to simplify estate planning and encourage Nigerians to take responsibility for how their assets were managed after death.
“At its core, will writing is about clarity, putting structure around what you have worked for, and giving those who depend on your greater certainty,” he said.
Olaiya stressed the importance of planning ahead, with biblical allusion to Isaiah 38:1, “Set your house in order”,  and Proverbs 13:22, ” A good man leaves inheritance for his children’s children”.
According to him, even the Holy Qur’an supports estate planning, as it encourages individuals to prepare their “Wasiya”, settle obligations and protect their families.
He said many Nigerians worked hard to build homes, businesses and savings, yet postponed decisions on how such assets should be managed.
“In our culture, speaking about a will can feel uncomfortable, but making one gives clarity, preserves peace and protects family dignity,” he said.
Olaiya said Castle eWill & Trust was created to change misconceptions about wills, noting that “writing a will does not mean expecting death, but taking responsibility for life.”
He said: “To some, wills are for the wealthy or elderly, but if anyone depends on you or you own anything, you need a plan.”
The legal practitioner added that assumptions that family members already understood one’s wishes could lead to disputes, stressing that written instructions provided stronger guidance.
“Do not leave your family to interpret your silence. Your legacy is not just assets, but the order and peace you leave behind,” he said.
Olaiya said the platform allowed users to organise their wishes, explore estate planning options and access guidance on wills, trusts and probate matters.
He said the platform included security features such as data encryption, identity verification and QR code authentication for wills.
“Every file is encrypted, identity is verified, and each Will generated carries a QR code to confirm authenticity and version history,” he said.
He added that users were prompted to review their wills periodically or after major life events such as marriage, childbirth or property acquisition.
Olaiya also addressed concerns within the legal profession, noting that the platform would not replace lawyers but expand opportunities.
“We are not trying to divide an existing cake, but to bake a bigger one by increasing estate planning adoption in Nigeria,” he said.
He noted that with over 200 million Nigerians and about 125 million adults, only a small percentage currently engaged in estate planning.
The Chairman, Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) Ikeja Branch, Mr Adeniyi Quadri, commended the founders of the initiative noting that technology had become inevitable in modern legal practice.
Quadri, who was represented by Mr Ayodeji Olabiwonnu, the General Secretary of the NBA, Ikeja Branch, noted that resistance to technology among legal practitioners was gradually fading, as digital tools were proving to enhance productivity rather than replace lawyers.
“Technology has come to stay, and lawyers do not have a choice but to embrace it. Every aspect of our practice is being transformed,” he said.
He said that platforms like Castle eWill and Trust could help address low adoption of estate planning in Nigeria by simplifying the process for individuals.
Mr Abiodun Fari-Arole, the Special Adviser to Ogun governor on housing, described the platform as innovative.
Fari-Arole emphasised the need for legal validity, safeguards and secure custody of executed wills.
Also in his remarks, Mr Adejare Olaoluwa, a Financial Executive and former Managing Director, Bank of Industry, called for professional safeguards and certification to boost public confidence in digital estate planning platforms.
Olaoluwa urged legal professionals to embrace technology, noting that digital transformation was inevitable.
“Technology will impact every profession. It is better to embrace it than resist it,” he said.
Also speaking, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria and former NBA General Secretary, Mr Dele Adesina, emphasised the sensitivity of wills and the need for strong security measures.
He said: “A will is a delicate instrument, and access must be strictly controlled to prevent disputes.”
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that highlight of the ceremony was a demonstration of the platform, as stakeholders expressed optimism about its potential to transform estate planning in Nigeria. (NAN)
Edited by Kevin Okunzuwa

Syria has called for an “independent and transparent” investigation into the sinking of a cargo ship in the Black Sea, demanding answers over the fate of the ship’s 10 crew members, including nine Syrians and an Egyptian, who remain unaccounted for.
The Togolese-flagged Alfa Watan,  went down  in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone early on Tuesday, amid a rising number of drone strikes hitting Black Sea shipping during the Russia-Ukraine war.
Recommended Stories

list 2 of 3  Ukraine says Russian drone attack sinks ship in Romanian waters
list 3 of 3  Russian strike on ship near Odesa kills 10, Ukraine hits Moscow with drones
end of list
It is unclear who carried out the attack.
Mazen Aloush, from the Syria’s port authority asked the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and Bulgarian authorities to find out why a  search and rescue mission  was called off, before the missing sailors were found.
“Their fate is still unknown” said Aloush, adding that “the reasons that led to the suspension of search and rescue operations” had to be established.
The attack on Tuesday also hit the Palau-flagged Able, setting it ablaze. Eighteen Turkish and Indian crew members were rescued from the burning vessel, while the Alfa Watan sank.
Both commercial ships were managed by Turkey-based companies, according to the Equasis merchant shipping database.
The Syrian sailors’ union said contact with the ship’s crew had been lost and no survivors had been found after search operations were halted.
The fire-damaged “Royad Mammadov” ship in the Black Sea after a fire aboard the vessel outside Romania’s territorial waters left two people dead on October 5 2026 [Reuters]   Aloush condemned the targeting of a civilian commercial vessel saying it was a serious breach of maritime security and a threat to sailors.

items.title: Mulheres vendem pedras na EN7 expostas ao perigo

original_payload.original_title: Mulheres vendem pedras na EN7 expostas ao perigo
original_payload.original_body:
Ao longo da Estrada Nacional Número 7 (EN7), no troço que liga a cidade de Tete ao município de Moatize, várias mulheres encontram na venda de pedras uma fonte de sustento para as suas famílias. Sob o sol, expostas aos riscos do trânsito, passam os dias à espera de clientes, numa actividade que, apesar das dificuldades, tem permitido melhorar as condições de vida dos seus agregados familiares.
É o caso de Crecia Castro, mãe de cinco filhos, que há seis anos se dedica à venda de pedras em Moatize. A actividade permitiu-lhe adquirir electrodomésticos e assegurar a frequência escolar dos filhos, graças ao rendimento obtido ao longo dos anos.
Entretanto, a vendedora afirma que o negócio já não apresenta o mesmo movimento de outros tempos, devido à redução do número de clientes, situação que dificulta a satisfação das necessidades básicas da família.
A diminuição das vendas representa um desafio para mulheres que dependem exclusivamente desta actividade para garantir a alimentação, a educação dos filhos e outras despesas domésticas. Com uma experiência de dez anos no mesmo ramo, Rita Manuel também conhece os desafios da profissão. Apesar das dificuldades, a venda de pedras permitiu-lhe construir a sua própria casa, um resultado que considera fruto do esforço e da persistência ao longo de uma década.
Além da redução da procura, as vendedeiras enfrentam diariamente os riscos associados à proximidade da estrada, onde a circulação constante de viaturas constitui uma ameaça à sua segurança. Entre Tete e Moatize, os montes de pedras expostos à beira da EN7 representam mais do que uma actividade comercial informal.
São o reflexo do esforço de mulheres que encontram no trabalho diário uma forma de sustentar as famílias e conquistar melhores condições de vida, mesmo perante a diminuição das vendas e os perigos a que estão expostas.

When did you realise that something was wrong with your reproductive health?
I was 15 when I started experiencing abdominal pain that lasted about four to five days every month. The pain occurred regularly, and I endured it for about three years before seeking medical attention.

Parmi eux figurait Nan Hasra Sylvain, alias Obama, qui a finalement succombé à ses blessures ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026. Ce nouvel décès porte à deux le nombre de victimes décédées dans cet accident.

items.title: Cure Sallé 2026 : Une grande course des dromadaires et des chevaux pour agrémenter les festivités

original_payload.original_title: Cure Sallé 2026 : Une grande course des dromadaires et des chevaux pour agrémenter les festivités
original_payload.original_body:
Par Nassirou Abdou Koulassan, Envoyé Spécial de l’ANP
Ingall, 3 octobre (ANP) – La grande course des dromadaires et des chevaux entrant dans le cadre des festivités de la 59 ème  édition de la Cure Salée a eu lieu ce samedi 3 octobre 2026. Elle est l’un des événements culturels majeurs de cette rencontre des pasteurs nomades, qui illustre la richesse des traditions nigériennes.
Cette course, ancrée dans le patrimoine local, ne se limite pas à une compétition sportive, mais constitue un véritable moment de rassemblement social et culturel.
La Cure Salée, note-t-on en effet, est une festivité qui célèbre les valeurs communautaires, la cohésion sociale et la préservation des pratiques ancestrales. La course des dromadaires, en tant qu’élément central de cette célébration, met en lumière l’importance des animaux dans la vie quotidienne et culturelle des populations nomades et rurales du Niger.
Cet événement attire non seulement les participants locaux mais aussi des visiteurs et passionnés de la culture saharienne, contribuant ainsi à la promotion du tourisme culturel et au développement économique régional. En outre, il favorise la transmission des savoir-faire traditionnels aux jeunes générations, garantissant la pérennité de ce patrimoine immatériel.
Les chevaux courent une distance de 8 kilomètres, les petits chameaux courent une distance de 10 kilomètres, et les grands chameaux courent des distances de 15 kilomètres.
La cérémonie a été marquée par la remise de prix pour les différentes catégories de la course. Catégorie chevaux : le vainqueur a reçu une enveloppe de 1 000 000 FCFA, le deuxième une enveloppe de 750 000 FCFA, la troisième place une enveloppe de 500 000 FCFA, le quatrième une enveloppe de 300 000 FCFA, et le cinquième une enveloppe de 200 000 FCFA.
Catégorie petits chameaux : le vainqueur a reçu une enveloppe de 750 000 FCFA, le deuxième une enveloppe de 500 000 FCFA, le troisième une enveloppe de 300 000 FCFA, le quatrième une enveloppe de 200 000 FCFA, et le cinquième une enveloppe de 150 000 FCFA.
Catégorie grands chameaux : le vainqueur a reçu une enveloppe de 1 500 000 FCFA, le deuxième une enveloppe de 1 000 000 FCFA, le troisième une enveloppe de 750 000 FCFA, le quatrième une enveloppe de 500 000 FCFA, et le cinquième une enveloppe de 300 000 FCFA.
La cérémonie a également été l’occasion pour l’Union des nigériens pour la vigilance et le patriotisme (UNVP) de remettre un chameau au Président de la République, Son Excellence le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, et un chameau au Premier Ministre, Son Excellence Monsieur Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine.
NAK/KPM/ANP-042 Octobre 2026

items.title: Xiong'an Forges a Complete Aerospace and Satellite Internet Ecosystem

original_payload.original_title: Xiong'an Forges a Complete Aerospace and Satellite Internet Ecosystem
original_payload.original_body:
English News
Xiong'an Forges a Complete Aerospace and Satellite Internet Ecosystem
Xiong'an New Area is rapidly developing its aerospace information and satellite internet industries, establishing a full-cycle ecosystem spanning R&D, manufacturing, testing, and in-orbit applications.
Alwihda Info
13 oct. 2026
The Honghu-03 satellite, also known as Xiong'an-1, was successfully launched into orbit aboard a Zhuque-3 Y2 reusable rocket from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone, Aug. 19. (Photo/Wang Weiqian)
Par Shao Yuzi, People's Daily
Xiong'an New Area in north China's Hebei province is accelerating the development of its aerospace information and satellite internet industries. A growing industrial ecosystem now covers research and development, manufacturing, testing, launch, and in-orbit applications.
The latest milestone came on Aug. 19, when the Honghu-03 satellite, also known as Xiong'an-1, was successfully launched into orbit aboard a Zhuque-3 Y2 reusable rocket from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in Jiuquan, northwest China.
At the satellite intelligent operation and management center of Hongqing—China's only fully integrated satellite constellation solution provider with full ecosystem capabilities—located in the pilot production base of the Xiong'an Science and Technology Innovation Center, staff members erupted in cheers as telemetry signals from Xiong'an-1 appeared on a large display screen.
As the first satellite developed and launched by Xiong'an New Area to enter orbit, Xiong'an-1 incorporates dozens of advanced technologies. Its successful launch marked the completion of a full-cycle industrial chain in the aerospace information and satellite internet sectors of Xiong'an New Area, spanning research and development, manufacturing, and in-orbit applications.
Just a few years ago, aerospace information and satellite internet were still relatively new concepts in Xiong'an. In 2021, China Satellite Network Group Co., Ltd. (China SatNet) was established there. In October 2024, the group officially relocated its headquarters to Xiong'an New Area. As a "chain leader" tasked with spearheading China's development of aerospace information and satellite internet, the company has generated strong demonstration and spillover effects.
"China SatNet is here, so we came here too. Being closer to the chain leader helps us iterate our products faster," said Chen Wei, chairman of CHIP LINKING INNO, a company focused on the R&D and production of high-end optoelectronic devices.
Chen spent more than a decade conducting research at the Institute of Semiconductors under the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Sensing an opportunity in the emerging industry, he led a team to Xiong'an in 2023 to advance the R&D and production of key components for satellite laser communications, including lasers, amplifiers, and communication modules.
When Chen started his business in Xiong'an, the aerospace information and satellite internet industries were still in their infancy, with a relatively weak industrial foundation. What gave him confidence, however, were the new area's clear and forward-looking industrial planning, supportive policies for talent, and full-cycle services for businesses.
"Xiong'an connects innovation with industry. Companies across the upstream and downstream segments are gathering and developing here, and there will be even more platform resources in the future," Chen said.
Today, CHIP LINKING INNO is far from the only company that has made its way to Xiong'an.
At the pilot production base of the Xiong'an Science and Technology Innovation Center, technicians at the satellite intelligent manufacturing workshop of Blue Arrow Hongqing (Xiong'an) Space Technology Co., Ltd. were testing a visual recognition system on an intelligent production line. Hongqing is currently applying AI and other emerging technologies to continuously improve production-line efficiency.
The development of industrial platforms is advancing in parallel. Equipment installation and commissioning have been completed at a shared satellite intelligent manufacturing center and a shared satellite testing center in the second phase of the pilot production base. Nearby, construction is also moving ahead on a satellite super factory and a supporting base for the final assembly of commercial satellites.
"Once these industrial platforms become operational by the end of this year, Xiong'an will have the capacity to produce 300 satellites annually," said an official with the industry, information technology, science and technology, and data bureau of Xiong'an New Area.
"Xiong'an New Area has made aerospace information and satellite internet the first industrial chain to receive priority deployment. We are creating favorable conditions, building platforms, opening up application scenarios, providing policy support, improving the business environment, and upgrading services to attract more companies and foster industrial clustering," the official told People's Daily.
"Our goal is to build Xiong'an into an important source of innovation for China's commercial space industry and satellite internet sector, as well as a key supplier for the development of low-Earth-orbit constellations," the official added.
Innovation resources are also rapidly gathering. Xiong'an is now home to 69 companies across the aerospace information industrial chain and nine innovation platforms.
As one of China's pilot cities for the large-scale application of the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS), Xiong'an is also making active use of aerospace information technologies to support urban development and accelerate the rollout of "BeiDou+" applications.
At a smart construction site in the start-up area of Xiong'an New Area, construction equipment such as road rollers and asphalt pavers are equipped with the BDS. They can automatically plan their routes and adjust their operating pace, with positioning accuracy controlled to within centimeters.
Baiyangdian Lake, the largest freshwater lake on the North China Plain, is another example. In Anxin county, all 24 rural tourism piers and more than 1,500 vessels have been equipped with dedicated BeiDou terminals. High-precision BeiDou positioning enables continuous monitoring of vessel movements and intelligent scheduling of water-based tourism services.
Today, "satellite internet + BeiDou" is being applied in a range of scenarios in Xiong'an, including underground spaces, smart construction sites, and the low-altitude economy.
And BeiDou is only one part of the picture. An increasing number of aerospace information technologies are being put to practical use in Xiong'an.
Recently, CHIP LINKING INNO's research team joined forces with a payload company in the new area to explore ways of bringing laser communications "from the sky to the ground."
Baiyangdian Lake is dotted with numerous scattered islands, making it difficult to lay fiber-optic cables between them. The team is therefore building laser communication links to replace fiber optics, with a transmission range of up to 10 kilometers.
"Satellite internet technology is bringing about a transformation from the sky to the ground," Chen said.
Looking ahead, his team will continue to tackle key technologies for ultra-high-speed laser communications while exploring a wider range of applications, with the aim of bringing the benefits of satellite internet technology to households across the country.
original_payload.original_summary: Xiong'an New Area is rapidly developing its aerospace information and satellite internet industries, establishing a full-cycle ecosystem spanning R&D, manufacturing, testing, and in-orbit applications.
