original_payload.original_title: Ex-student offers N5m scholarships, rewards teachers in Enugu
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Ex-student offers N5m scholarships, rewards teachers in Enugu
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   9 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Alex Enebeli
A former student of St. Patrick’s Secondary School, Obollo-Afor, Enugu State, Noel Alumona, has launched a five-year fund worth N5 million to support students and reward teachers.
The fund, known as the Noel Ifeanyi Alumona Impact Fund, offers scholarships and awards to students and teachers of the school.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the school, located in Udenu Local Government Area of Enugu State, is owned and managed by the Catholic Diocese of Nsukka.
The 2026 edition featured three categories: One-Year Full Scholarship Based on Financial Needs, Excellence Impact Awards and Outstanding Teachers Awards.
Six students received one-year full scholarships based on financial needs. They are Chidiebere Victory, Zita Ogbonna, Chukwuemeka Victor, Catherine Egwu, Shadrach Nnaji and Elias Eze.
The Excellence Impact Awards recognised Chukwujekwu Faith as the best student in Science and Martha Odo as the best in Arts and Humanities.
Mercy Nnaji received the Rising Scholar Award, while Faith Agbedo won the Student Community Impact Award.
The Outstanding Teachers Awards went to Mrs Mary Obule, Mrs Elizabeth Ugwu and Mrs Amos-Glory Obinna, who each received N100,000.
Speaking at the launch, the School Administrator, Rev. Fr. Eric Uroko, said the initiative would help indigent students complete their secondary education and motivate teachers to remain committed to their work.
Uroko said six students received full scholarships covering their three school terms, while four others were recognised for their academic achievements and community service.
He said the initiative demonstrated the importance of giving back to one’s roots and creating opportunities for younger generations.
“In Noel Alumona, we do not just see a benefactor; we see a son of the soil who was shaped by activities that took place here several years ago.
“This invaluable exercise he embarked on, starting from today, emphasises his decision that the footprints he left behind should serve as a staircase for those coming after.
“It tells struggling students that their dreams matter. It tells dedicated teachers that their time at the laboratory, library, and classrooms are valued,” he said.
Uroko said Alumona’s journey from the classroom to international platforms had been inspiring, citing his contributions to humanitarian work, youth development and equity.
He said Alumona had supported vulnerable children and children with disabilities through his Hope for African Children Initiative and Boys Champions.
He added that Alumona had also promoted healthy masculinity among young men and encouraged respect for women and girls as part of efforts to end gender-based violence.
Earlier, Alumona, an international award winner and founder of the Boys Champions Foundation, said the initiative was designed to promote academic excellence, reward dedicated teachers and encourage students to take their education seriously.
He said the fund would also mobilise former students to contribute to the school’s infrastructural and academic development.
Alumona attributed his achievements to the foundation he received at the school, describing the fund as a way of giving back to an institution that helped shape his future.
“St. Patrick’s made me. Whatever I see myself doing today is because of the foundation I had in St. Patrick’s.
“If you have ever been in doubt that the work you are doing as teachers is not productive, I think you have one story now to share.
“The work you do here is productive, and we are grateful for the hard work and upbringing you continue to give these children,” he said.
Alumona said his interest in humanitarian work began in Senior Secondary School Two (SS2), when he established his first non-profit organisation, Youth for Change.
He said plans were underway to introduce another award category in 2027 to recognise teachers who had served the institution for more than 20 years.
One of the beneficiaries, Mrs Amos-Glory Obinna, commended Alumona for the recognition, saying it would motivate her and other recipients to do more.
“I feel so grateful for receiving this wonderful award as the best staff of St. Patrick’s Secondary School. I also want to thank our sponsor for appreciating the staff and remembering his root,” she said.
The highlight of the event was the presentation of an award to Alumona by the school in recognition of his generosity and commitment to education. (NAN)

items.title: L'AfCRA, une agence de notation africaine pour contrer les biais des géants mondiaux

original_payload.original_title: L'AfCRA, une agence de notation africaine pour contrer les biais des géants mondiaux
original_payload.original_body:
Moody's, Fitch, S&P... et maintenant l'AfCRA. L'Agence  africaine  de notation de crédit, spécifique au continent, sera inaugurée le 7 octobre à Port-Louis, capitale de l'Ile Maurice, où se trouve son siège.
Développée par l' Union africaine  mais conçue comme une institution indépendante, l'AfCRA a pour but d'offrir une évaluation du risque de crédit mieux adaptée aux réalités africaines et de faciliter l'accès à l'emprunt sur les marchés internationaux, qui demeure très difficile et cher pour un grand nombre de pays du continent.
Un sujet sensible qui vaut de vives critiques aux grandes agences de notation financière, accusées d'exagérer les risques liés au crédit dans les pays africains, contribuant ainsi au maintien de taux élevés, qui nuisent à leur développement.
À lire aussi  Sommet "Africa Forward" : il "faut changer le regard" sur la question du financement en Afrique
Des crédits jusqu'à quatre fois plus chers que dans l'UE
Pour évaluer le risque de crédit, les agences de notation se basent sur plusieurs facteurs parmi lesquels la performance économique du pays, la qualité de la gouvernance, sa solvabilité ou bien encore ses capacités de résilience face aux crises.
Ces analyses donnent lieu à l'attribution de notes : allant de triple ou double AA, selon les agences, à C ou D. Des notes qui ne définissent pas à elles seules les taux de crédits auxquels les États et les entreprises peuvent emprunter mais qui les influencent fortement.
Or l' Afrique  demeure largement exclue de ce système. Parmi les 54 pays du continent, 22 n'ont tout simplement pas été évaluées par les grandes agences de notation et ne possèdent donc aucune note souveraine.
Les autres, très majoritairement, évoluent entre les notes B et C (de crédit très risqué à défaut de paiement) contre A/A+ en moyenne dans l'UE (crédit de qualité supérieure moyenne). Résultat : des taux de crédit moyens avoisinant 4 % dans l'UE mais près de 7 % en Afrique de l'Ouest, 12 % en Afrique centrale et même 14 % en Afrique de l'Est.
À cela s'ajoutent souvent des primes de risques pour les petites et moyennes entreprises, jugées moins solides, qui leur compliquent encore l'accès au crédit.
Une situation intenable qui constitue l'un des principaux freins au développement du continent, selon de nombreux experts.
Pour afficher ce contenu YouTube, il est nécessaire d'autoriser les cookies de mesure d'audience et de publicité.

items.title: PARTIELLEMENT FAUX : Cette image d’un pont au Tchad n’a pas été générée par l’intelligence artificielle

original_payload.original_title: PARTIELLEMENT FAUX : Cette image d’un pont au Tchad n’a pas été générée par l’intelligence artificielle
original_payload.original_body:
La photo illustre l’inauguration d’un pont sur l’axe Gagal-Koimbi, dans la province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, au Tchad.
Ce   post sur TikTok  , qui affirme que cette image d’un pont inauguré au Tchad a été générée par l’IA, est PARTIELLEMENT FAUX.
Le post publié le 11 octobre 2026 prétend apporter un démenti à une image présentée comme l’inauguration d’un pont au Tchad. L’auteur du post affirme notamment que l’image a été générée par l’IA. « Ce sont les haineux de l’AES qui ont produit cette image avec l’intelligence artificielle pour dénigrer le Tchad, parce que le Tchad ne fait plus partie de leur histoire de fausse souveraineté. Il faut dire à Ibrahim Traoré que sa haine envers les pays qui ne partagent pas leur vision est vouée à l’échec », ajoute-t-il.
PesaCheck a examiné ce post et l’a trouvé partiellement faux.
Une   recherche d’images inversée   sur Google Lens a permis à PesaCheck de savoir que la photo est authentique, contrairement à ce qu’affirme l’auteur de la publication examinée.
Selon Alwihda Info, la photo a été prise le 9 octobre 2026 et illustre   l’inauguration d’un pont sur l’axe Gagal-Koimbi  , dans la province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, au Tchad.
Pour le média   tchad.com   , le pont a été réalisé par   la population de Koimbi   à l’aide des matériaux traditionnels, notamment du bois. Il s’agit d’une initiative motivée par la dégradation du pont sur l’axe Gagal-Koimbi.
Cette information est corroborée   ici  .
L’auteur du post en examen a également présenté une autre image, comme un pont inauguré au Tchad.
Une   recherche d’images inversée   sur Google Lens a permis à PesaCheck de trouver la   photo   dans un article publié le 2 décembre 2025.
Selon le média Tribune Echos, elle a été prise le 1 er  décembre 2025 lors  de  l’inauguration du Pont de la refondation  . Il s’agit du   troisième pont   de la ville de N’Djamena au Tchad.
Cette information est corroborée   ici   et   ici  .
Les deux images présentées dans la publication examinée ont toutes été prises dans des villes et à des périodes différentes au Tchad. Elles sont authentiques et aucune d’elles n’a été générée par l’IA.
PesaCheck a examiné une publication sur TikTok affirmant qu’une image d’un pont inauguré au Tchad avait été générée par l’IA et a conclu qu’elle était PARTIELLEMENT FAUSSE.
Cette publication fait partie d’une série continue de vérifications des faits par PesaCheck, examinant du contenu marqué comme une  désinformation potentielle  sur Facebook et d’autres plateformes de médias sociaux.
En établissant un partenariat avec Facebook et des plateformes de médias sociaux similaires    , les organisations tierces de vérification des faits comme PesaCheck aident à faire le tri entre les faits et la fiction. Nous faisons ceci en donnant au public, un aperçu plus profond et un contexte aux publications qu’il voit dans ses flux de médias sociaux.
Avez-vous repéré ce que vous pensez être une fausse information sur Facebook ?     Voici comment vous pouvez le signaler    . Et     voici     plus d’informations sur     la méthodologie de PesaCheck     pour vérifier les contenus douteux.
Cette vérification de faits a été rédigée par le fact-checker      Youssoufa Mahamadou      et éditée par      Josaphat Finogbé     , éditeur d’articles à PesaCheck. Cet article a été approuvé pour publication par le rédacteur principal à PesaCheck,      Stephen Ndegwa     .
PesaCheck est la première initiative de vérification des faits des finances publiques en Afrique. Il a été cofondé par      Catherine Gicheru      et      Justin Arenstein      et est incubé par le plus grand accélérateur de technologies civiques et de journalisme de données du continent:      Code for Africa     . Il vise à aider le public à séparer la réalité de la fiction dans les déclarations publiques sur les chiffres qui façonnent notre monde, avec un accent particulier sur les déclarations sur les finances publiques qui façonnent la prestation par le gouvernement des services publics liés aux objectifs de développement durable (ODD), tels que les soins de santé, le développement rural et l’accès à l’eau / à l’assainissement.      PesaCheck      teste également l’exactitude des reportages médiatiques. Pour en savoir plus sur le projet, visitez      pesacheck.org     .
Envoyez-nous un email
Contactez-nous sur WhatsApp
PesaCheck est une initiative conjointe de      Code for Africa     , à travers son      fonds InnovateAFRICA     , avec un soutien de la      Deutsche Welle Akademie     , en partenariat avec une coalition de médias locaux africains et d’autres organisations civiques de surveillance.

items.title: Hegseth says firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter will be ‘public’

original_payload.original_title: Hegseth says firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter will be ‘public’
original_payload.original_body:
United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said the execution of a former US Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in Texas will be publicly available to watch.
In an interview with the media outlet Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Hegseth was asked about President Donald Trump’s recent order to use a firing squad to execute Nidal Hasan, who was convicted of the 2009 shooting.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Fort Hood shooting trial begins
list 2 of 3  Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood attacker Nidal Hasan
list 3 of 3  Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad: All to know
end of list
The secretary said he approved of the decision, calling it a “no-brainer”.
“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public,” Hegseth told interviewer Jack Posobiec. “Because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things.”
Hegseth added that the execution would take place at Fort Hood on December 3 at 1pm US Central Time (19:00 GMT), the same time that the 2009 shooting took place.
Hasan was  sentenced  to death in August 2013 after a military jury found him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted murder for the shooting.
The former Army major walked into an army processing centre on the Texas base, shouted “Allahu akbar” (God is greatest) and opened fire on fellow military members waiting to get medical attention.
Hasan’s execution required approval from Hegseth and Trump, who authorised the use of the firing squad on Monday.
An official with the Defense Department told Al Jazeera that Hasan’s execution would be “livestreamed”, adding that more details would come soon.
It is not clear from Hegseth’s remarks whether troops, spectators or US military officials would be present in person for the execution. US Army regulation states that at least two media outlets should be selected as witnesses.

items.title: Group calls on FG, stakeholders to end early girl child marriage

original_payload.original_title: Group calls on FG, stakeholders to end early girl child marriage
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Group calls on FG, stakeholders to end early girl child marriage
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   2 hours ago   ·  Updated  28 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
oplus_0
✓
✓
By Kennedy Sheyin
A Non-governmental Organisation (NGO), the Tabitha Cumi Foundation (TCF), has called for the abolishment of early girl child marriage in Nigeria.
The TCF made the call on Thursday in Abuja, at the commemoration of the International Day of Girl Child through the Girls Rights, Education and Protection (G-REAP) project, funded by the Ford Foundation.
The event has as its theme “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights”.
Speaking at the event, the Executive Director, TCF, Mrs Adetayo Erinle, acknowledged the existing policies already in place by the government to curb child marriage in Nigeria, and commended the government for enacting them.
Erinle represented by the Programme Manager, Mrs Nendirmwe Ohah, said this was because the government had a key role to play in ending child marriage in the country through formulating the right policies.
“There are the laws enacted to prevent gender based violence, and many of them are even under review to capture emerging issues around technology facilitated gender based violence and other forms of abuse”, she said.
She commended the development and all stakeholders that have worked towards the review and updating of the laws to capture the evolving nature of gender based violence in recent times.
She however, emphasised that fruition of the policies required the government to go beyond formulation of policies to seeing that the policies were properly implemented.
“The government has the responsibility of implementing and enforcing these laws, especially in the communities where the practice of child marriage is predominant.
“This way, these laws translate to communities where girls can feel safe, respected and supported.
“We need to work together to create communities where girls are heard and live up to their full potential,” she said.
The executive director also called on parents, schools, religious environments, social groups and all stakeholders involved in raising girls to create awareness and facilitate safer environment for girls in their social communities.
“The foundation is doing its part, but we cannot do it alone. Everyone needs to put hands together to create environments that don’t breed abuse, but help protect girls and aid them achieve their individual goals,” she added.
Mrs Sonaya Adeniyi-Fashola, Girls Rights Activist and guest speaker at the event, called on stakeholders in the society to allow girl children have options to choose from, instead of marrying them off at very young ages.
According to Adeniyi-Fashola, early marriage stunts the growth of young girls, preventing them from actualising their dreams, while also putting them at health risk due to possible early child bearing complications.
She called for young girls to be empowered, educated on their rights and allowed to go to schools and live their lives at their own pace, noting that when girls mature before marriage, they blossom.
“We should invest in them, give them scholarships, equip them with skills, give them the right exposure and enable them to become financially independent and educated,” she said.
She commended the TCF for the initiative and called on other groups to borrow a leaf from the organisation and do everything possible to eradicate early child marriage, while empowering girls where necessary.
She added that another key tool towards curbing child marriage was awareness.
“Firstly, the girls need to be aware of their rights and the laws that protect them from being married off at young ages.
“The parents also need to be aware of the possible trauma and health complications that could come from child marriage and it’s permanent consequences on the girl child,” she said.
She also called on the government to strengthen implementation of laws that prevented young girls from being married off, noting that strict adherence would result to visible change in society.
Mrs Nafisah Kote, Officer, Gender Unit, FCT Universal Basic Education Board, said that the board was working actively with relevant stakeholders to raise stable and confident girls.
She urged the beneficiaries to extend the knowledge gained from the educative session to their fellow girls that were not opportuned to be present.
Kote also commended the TCF for the initiative to assist the government and called on other groups to join in and support the already existing efforts, noting that it takes all hands to raise empowered, stable, confident girls.( NAN )
Edited by Deborah Coker

items.title: 3è session ordinaire de la commission consultative 2026 de la Ville de Maradi : Dégager des orientations pour la bonne marche de la collectivité

original_payload.original_title: 3è session ordinaire de la commission consultative 2026 de la Ville de Maradi : Dégager des orientations pour la bonne marche de la collectivité
original_payload.original_body:
Société
3è session ordinaire de la commission consultative 2026 de la Ville de Maradi : Dégager des orientations pour la bonne marche de la collectivité
ONEP NE
9 octobre 2026
La table de séance à l’ouverture de la session
Partager vers les réseaux
La 3è session ordinaire de la commission consultative de la Ville de Maradi au titre de l’année 2026 a ouvert ses travaux, le mercredi 7 octobre 2026. Cette importante session s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’exercice régulier de la gouvernance locale.
A l’ouverture des travaux, l’administrateur délégué de la Ville de Maradi, Le Lieutenant-colonel Abdoulaye Moussa Garba, a indiqué que cette session leur offre une occasion d’examiner plusieurs dossiers sur le fonctionnement de la ville, la situation socio-économique des populations, le suivi de certaines opérations d’intérêt public ainsi que la programmation budgétaire de l’exercice 2027. « En tant que cadre de concertation et d’examen des questions intéressant la vie de la collectivité, la commission consultative doit permettre d’apprécier avec objectivité les situations qui lui sont soumises, de recueillir les observations des différents acteurs et contribuer à la formulation d’orientation adaptées aux réalités de notre ville », a-t-il averti.
Plusieurs points sont inscrits à l’ordre du jour et demandent de la part des conseillers, rigueur, responsabilité, esprit de concertation et sens élevé d’intérêt général. Il s’agit de la lecture et l’amendement du procès-verbal de la précédente session extraordinaire, la situation de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, la situation de la campagne agricole et la distribution gratuite des vivres ; la situation sur le déguerpissement des occupants de Kadiro ; le compte rendu de la mission de l’administrateur délégué à Agadez et la présentation et l’adoption du budget 2027.
« De la qualité de vos travaux dépendra notre capacité collective à examiner les dossiers avec objectivité, à faire ressortir les préoccupations essentielles et à dégager des orientations susceptibles de contribuer efficacement à la bonne marche de notre collectivité », a reconnu l’administrateur délégué de la Ville de Maradi. Il a enfin demandé aux conseillers d’aborder les différents points inscrits à l’ordre du jour avec un esprit de responsabilité, de concertation et de service public.
Intervenant à son tour, le gouverneur de la région de Maradi, le Contrôleur Général de Police Mamane Issoufou a estimé que tous les points inscrits à l’ordre du jour sont pertinents. C’est pourquoi, il a insisté sur la participation assidue des conseillers aux débats sur ces questions et leur a demandé d’adopter un budget réaliste pour l’année 2027.

original_payload.original_title: En RDC, Amnesty International lance une campagne pour lutter contre l'impunité
original_payload.original_body:
En RDC, Amnesty International lance une campagne pour lutter contre l'impunité
En République démocratique du Congo, Amnesty International lance, jeudi 1er octobre, une campagne contre l'impunité, intitulée « Six millions de voix pour la justice au Congo ». Elle vise à sensibiliser le public, par le biais d'une pétition, mais aussi les responsables politiques, les diplomates et les représentants onusiens, afin de mettre en place des mécanismes judiciaires pour juger les exactions commises ces 30 dernières années, principalement dans l'est du pays.
Publié le :  01/10/2026 - 15:45
Le logo d'Amnesty International est visible dans ses locaux de Hong Kong en octobre 2021. (Image d'illustration)        AFP - ISAAC LAWRENCE
Par :
RFI
Avec notre correspondante à Kinshasa ,    Paulina Zidi
Six millions : c'est le nombre de victimes des différents conflits dans l'est de la   RDC   depuis 30 ans retenu par Amnesty International. Un des responsables de la campagne explique néanmoins que ce chiffre est avant tout symbolique, car il n'existe pas officiellement de bilan. Ce qui compte, selon l'organisation, c'est qu'un mort d'un conflit est toujours un mort de trop.
Six millions de voix, c'est aussi le nombre de signatures attendues pour la pétition. Elle réclame la mise en place de mécanismes internationalisés, c'est-à-dire capables de juger au Congo les crimes internationaux.

items.title: NAF recovers more wreckage from Ondo aircraft crash

original_payload.original_title: NAF recovers more wreckage from Ondo aircraft crash
original_payload.original_body:
THE Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has recovered additional components from its ATR 42-500 aircraft that crashed in Igbokoda, Ondo State, as multi-agency teams continue search and recovery operations at the accident site.
In a statement  posted  on its official X handle on Wednesday, the Air Force said specialist divers from the Nigerian Navy and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) continued underwater search and recovery operations alongside its recovery team.
“Additional aircraft components have been recovered as efforts continue to locate and retrieve relevant materials for documentation and preservation in support of the ongoing investigation,” the statement said.
The development comes amid growing concerns over the potential public health risks posed by the unrecovered bodies of the 25 people aboard the aircraft, with residents and the community’s traditional ruler warning that decomposing remains and possible fuel leaks could contaminate local water sources.
The monarch of Igbokoda, Afolabi Odidiomo, had raised the alarm over the persistent stench from the crash site and the possible pollution of a river connected to the community’s water supply.

items.title: Cleric urges 2027 election officials to reject inducements

original_payload.original_title: Cleric urges 2027 election officials to reject inducements
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  Cleric urges 2027 election officials to reject inducements
By  Nefisetu Yakubu   ·   2 hours ago   ·  6 min read
✓
✓
By EricJames Ochigbo
Rev. Fr. Robert Kajoh, a Catholic priest of the Missionary Society of St. Paul, has urged officials and stakeholders in the 2027 general elections to reject inducements and discharge their responsibilities with integrity.
Kajoh gave the advice in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on the sidelines of his 25th priestly anniversary in Abuja.
NAN ​‌‌‌‍‌​‍⁠⁠‍​⁠‍⁠​‌​‍‌​reports that St. Anselm Chaplaincy, Gwagwalada, organised the ceremony.
Kajoh served as its chaplain for 11 years before his posting to St. Mary Magdalene Catholic Parish, Humble, Texas, United States, in January.
The cleric cautioned voters and election workers against allowing financial incentives or material benefits to influence their decisions, warning that such rewards could undermine the country’s democratic future.
According to him, material rewards are temporary compared with the long-term consequences of compromising the nation’s future for personal gain.
Kajoh urged Nigerians to be content with what they had and resist compromising their values for money, saying sacrifices made for the common good would benefit future generations.
He called on Nigerians to embrace honesty, integrity and accountability, saying that if 20 per cent of the country’s population committed to doing what was right, the nation could transform within a short time.
“My hope is that election workers, as men and women of faith, will do the right thing, refuse to compromise or sell their conscience for money or material things, which are transient.
“If they are honest and do their jobs, rejecting inducements, they will preserve their integrity and trust that God will provide for them.
“No sacrifice is too great to secure a better future for our children and grandchildren. No amount of money is worth compromising our destiny.
“If people stand firmly for what is right, God, who provides for the birds of the air, will provide for them. We should be content with what we have and trust Him to increase our efforts,” he said.
Kajoh expressed gratitude for the opportunity to serve the community, describing his experience as evidence that his priestly calling had made a meaningful difference in people’s lives.
In his remarks, the Chaplain of St. Anselm Chaplaincy, Rev. Fr. Tony Bassey, described Kajoh as an intelligent, sociable, humble, hardworking and compassionate priest.
He urged leaders at all levels to embrace humility, compassion and teamwork while developing independence and critical thinking to address the needs of their followers.
“Kajoh works with people, he takes people along, and we need leadership that takes people along, that listens to people, and Kajoh is a compassionate person that cares for his parishioners; you can see how many people troop around him.
“So we need leaders in Nigeria that are very compassionate, that are down to earth, that feel the impulse, the pains, and the tears of the people and that are able to address them.
“Kajoh is also very sound, intelligent and analytical. We need leaders who are sound and intelligent, able to analyse issues for themselves.
“They should provide solutions to people’s challenges, not depend on others to think for them.
“Kajoh is a very prayerful person; we see him talk about righteousness, about prayer and so on. We need leaders who are very prayerful and pray for the nation.
“Not those who keep watch at night to think of how to steal from Nigeria, but those who pray and wish the good of Nigeria,” he said.
Also speaking, the Vice-Chairman of St. Anselm Chaplaincy Pastoral Council, Mr Joseph Eneji, said Kajoh left behind a vibrant chaplaincy.
Eneji said Kajoh built a community committed to prayer, spiritual growth and revival programmes, while establishing institutions that promoted devotion and worship.
“Kajoh was able to build lives that can handle their challenges through prayers to get solution.
“Kajoh was able to build hearts of the people at the Chaplaincy for God. He built a committed and vibrant Chaplaincy.
“He has impacted lives physically and spiritually, he has mentored many. Kajoh brought a lot of transformations to the chaplaincy and therefore, deserved every right to be celebrated.
“St. Anselm Chaplaincy was privileged to have Fr. Kajoh as a chaplain for more than decade, so celebrating his 25th priestly ordination anniversary is worth doing,” he said.
The celebrant’s mother, Mama Elizabeth Kajoh, expressed joy at witnessing what she described as God’s blessings in her life and the lives of her children.
Mama Kajoh urged young parents to ensure that families prayed and worshipped together in holiness, saying parents must set good examples for their children.
“I feel blessed, in fact, I keep asking God what have I done to deserve so much blessings; these blessings, I do not merit them.
“What is most effective is prayer. Prayer in the home is very important. If you do not pray with your children, when they go out there, they will not know what to do.
“The Lord has said that, ‘train a child in the way it should go, when he fires up, he will not part from it’; prayer is very, very important,” she said.
Dr Emmanuel Kajoh, the celebrant’s brother, prayed for God’s continued blessings and strength for the priest as he continued his ministry and prepared to celebrate more years of service.
“God will continue to bless and will continue to strengthen him, to continue to lead him, to continue to go before him to lead him, behind him to guide him, above him to keep and within to strengthen him, so that his ministry will continue to grow to win more souls.
“May God give him good health, long life, so that he will celebrate another 25 years,” he said.
A parishioner, Mrs Eunice Apochi, described Kajoh as a wonderful and spiritual priest who had positively impacted individuals and the worshipping community.
“He is a priest that has lifted me spiritually, he is my spiritual director; his prayer has touched lives, a lot of people have been healed through his prayer, we have had a lot of converts through his ministry, there is so much to say about him, actually.
“I wish that God will bless him, God will keep him, and God will grant him all that he needs for a very good life. And I also pray above all, that he will never regret being a servant of God,” she prayed.(NAN)

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : une opération de salubrité mobilise les forces de défense au lycée bilingue d'Am-Timan
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : une opération de salubrité mobilise les forces de défense au lycée bilingue d'Am-Timan
Alwihda Info
09 oct. 2026
Par Mahamat Abdelbanat Kourma
Les éléments de la zone de défense n° 10, sous le commandement du général Fourazi Hassane Mahamat, ont consacré la matinée de ce vendredi 9 octobre 2026 à une opération de salubrité au lycée bilingue d’Am-Timan.
Munis de pelles, de râteaux, de brouettes et de coupe-coupes, les éléments des forces de défense et de sécurité se sont mobilisés pour nettoyer l'enceinte de l'établissement. Le maire de la ville d'Am-Timan, Mahamat Ali Ibrahim, a également pris part à cette initiative.
Dès 6 h 30, le général Fourazi Hassane Mahamat et ses hommes ont investi la cour du lycée. Avant le début des travaux, le commandant a réuni ses éléments afin de les sensibiliser à l'importance de cette action citoyenne et à la nécessité de contribuer à l'assainissement des établissements scolaires.
Après les consignes, les soldats se sont mis au travail. Ils ont coupé les herbes qui avaient envahi la cour, ramassé les ordures et dégagé les différents espaces de l'établissement. L'objectif était de rendre le cadre scolaire plus propre, plus agréable et mieux adapté aux activités pédagogiques.
Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le commandant de la zone de défense n° 10 a indiqué que cette opération s'inscrivait dans le cadre de l'appel du chef de l'État, le maréchal Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno, invitant les citoyens à se mobiliser pour améliorer l'environnement des établissements scolaires.
De son côté, le proviseur du lycée bilingue d'Am-Timan, Allamine Ousmane, a exprimé sa reconnaissance aux forces de défense et de sécurité pour leur engagement. Il a salué une initiative qui contribue à l'amélioration du cadre de vie scolaire et des conditions d'apprentissage des élèves.
Au cours de cette matinée, les uniformes militaires étaient plus nombreux que les cartables dans la cour du lycée. À l'issue des travaux, l'établissement a retrouvé un environnement plus propre et dégagé, offrant ainsi aux lycéens un cadre plus accueillant pour poursuivre leur formation.

items.title: The state must do its share

original_payload.original_title: The state must do its share
original_payload.original_body:
Good afternoon. Mozambique’s government wants mining and energy investors to process more resources locally and buy more from Mozambican businesses. At this week’s CAVAME-d conference in Nacala, investors have been reminding it that factories also need reliable electricity and usable roads. The ambition is reasonable. Its credibility depends partly on what the government itself is prepared to deliver.
The complaint from Syrah Resources, which operates the Balama graphite mine, was concrete. Its representative described deteriorating road connections to Pemba and Nacala, and continued reliance on diesel generators. Further graphite processing would require dependable electricity. A company facing those constraints in its existing operation has good reason to question the economics of adding another stage of production.
The full Daily Briefing continues below for Pro subscribers. Subscribers to the  Zitamar News  tier can read the top half, including the full leader article,    here   .
Subscribe from just $12 a month
Nampula governor Eduardo Abdula identified roads and reliable energy among the priorities for industrial development. His intervention brought the discussion back to the conditions investors need before committing capital. These are responsibilities that public authorities must help fulfil, through investment, planning and coordination. Listing them at a conference is useful only if it leads to work that companies and communities can see.
Local content is meant to run both ways. The government has become more explicit about what Mozambique should receive from investors, including jobs, domestic purchases and a greater share of processing. It must be equally explicit about the services and infrastructure its own institutions will provide. Investors’ obligations can be written into contracts and legislation. The state’s commitments also need budgets, deadlines and institutions responsible for delivery.
There is a sound economic argument for retaining more value from Mozambique’s resources. Processing can create employment, expand the tax base and generate business for local suppliers. But those benefits depend on operations that can compete and find buyers. Requiring a mineral to be processed domestically does not remove the cost of unreliable power or difficult transport. Where those costs make production uncompetitive, an obligation on paper may produce little investment.

original_payload.original_body:
The Nigeria Medical Association, Kwara State chapter, has raised the alarm over alleged illegal salary deductions, poor remuneration and severe manpower shortages in the state’s public hospitals, warning that the conditions are exposing doctors to excessive workloads and burnout.
The state chairman of the association, Dr Suleiman Rotimi, disclosed this on Monday in Ilorin at a news conference organised as part of activities marking the 2026 Physicians’ Week, themed “Securing the Future of Medicine in Nigeria.”
Rotimi lamented that despite their critical role in the healthcare system, doctors in Kwara remained among the least paid in the country, with some facing monthly salary deductions running into tens of thousands of naira.
“The doctors are underpaid, overworked and over-deducted. Some doctors had between N30,000 and N50,000 deducted from their monthly salaries despite outstanding allowances and what he described as poor remuneration.”

original_payload.original_body:
Les élèves de l'école primaire d'Abena, dans le 7ᵉ arrondissement de N'Djamena, disposent désormais d'un cadre plus sûr. Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) a appuyé la réhabilitation de l'établissement par la construction d'un mur de clôture, dont les travaux ont été officiellement réceptionnés ce jeudi 22 octobre 2026. Cette réalisation s'inscrit dans les interventions du PNUD pour le renforcement de la résilience des communautés et l'amélioration des conditions d'apprentissage. Le PNUD a réaffirmé à cette occasion son engagement aux côtés des communautés tchadiennes, ainsi que son soutien aux efforts visant à améliorer les infrastructures éducatives et la qualité de l'environnement scolaire.

original_payload.original_body: C'est quand le glucose sanguin reste élevé plus longtemps que prévu que cela pourrait indiquer que le corps ne régule pas normalement le glucose, explique Sherr. Cela pourrait être un signe de résistance à l'insuline, où le corps ne réagit pas normalement au glucose. La résistance à l'insuline peut se produire si le corps est exposé à des niveaux élevés de sucre dans le sang pendant une longue période. À terme, cela peut conduire au prédiabète et au diabète de type 2. L'hyperglycémie persistante que connaissent certains diabétiques peut ensuite entraîner des complications, y compris des dommages aux nerfs et aux yeux, des maladies cardiaques et des AVC.

Ocasio-Cortez, who has become a progressive stalwart since her surprise 2018 congressional victory, confirmed the donation in a statement on Friday and a speech in Michigan. The transfer was first reported by the New York Times.

original_payload.original_title: Dakar prepares to host the 2026, Youth Olympics Africa’s first Olympic event
original_payload.original_body:
Youth
With just days to go, construction crews across Dakar are working around the clock preparing to welcome one of the biggest international events the city has ever hosted. The Senegalese capital will be hosting Africa’s first Olympic event when the Youth Olympics begin on October 31.
The Games will run until November 13 and will bring together about 2,700 young athletes to compete in 35 sports across Dakar and the nearby cities of Diamniadio and Saly. On the city’s corniche, skateboarders said they were excited to see the Games come to Africa.
“This is a first opportunity for Senegal and, by extension, for Africa, to discover new sports. It is the very first time that a major competition of this scale has come to Africa,” said student Thomas Dieme. Skateboarding will be making its debut at the Youth Olympics in Dakar this year. The sport has caught on with a small group of Senegalese youth, and skater Sete Awad said he hopes the Olympics will help them get more attention on the sport.
original_payload.original_summary: The countdown is on in Dakar. With just days to go, construction crews are racing against the clock to prepare Senegal’s capital for a historic global sporting event.

items.title: 2027: Rainbow Coalition promoting political stability, unity in FCT — Wike

original_payload.original_title: 2027: Rainbow Coalition promoting political stability, unity in FCT — Wike
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  2027: Rainbow Coalition promoting political stability, unity in FCT — Wike
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   1 hour ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Philip Yatai
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says his Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political platform, has promoted political stability and unity ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Wike said this on Friday during an interactive session with stakeholders from the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kuje Area Council.
Addressing party leaders, traditional rulers and community stakeholders, Wike said effective governance required political differences to be set aside in favour of public interest and tangible infrastructural development.
He highlighted the presence of APC and PDP members in the same hall to discuss community development, describing it as an example of cooperation rather than partisan conflict.
“If Nigerian politics can come to this level, we will not be hearing fighting; we will not be seeing ourselves killing each other.
“You can shout PDP today in the FCT, and at the same time, you can shout APC in the same hall. It is a collective coalition,” he said.
The minister said the bipartisan approach was designed to eliminate political discrimination and enable representatives across party lines to work together for residents and satellite towns.
He contrasted the administration’s achievements with previous political promises, urging citizens to assess leaders based on their records and hold them accountable for their performance.
Wike cautioned voters against political gamblers and online rhetoric, urging residents to focus on tangible achievements, including road construction, educational stability and local infrastructure development.
He cited projects in Kuje, including the completion and expansion of the Gwagwalada road network and the dualisation of Kuje-Airport Road, as evidence of the administration’s commitment.
“When President Bola Tinubu appointed us, he instructed us to go to the satellite towns and ask the people what their problems are.
“Making promises and fulfilling those promises, that is what representation and governance should be about,” the minister said.
Wike urged Kuje residents to support Tinubu’s re-election bid and extend similar support to Sen. Philip Aduda, who is seeking election to represent the FCT in the Senate.
He also called on residents to support Mr John Gabaya for AMAC-Bwari Federal Constituency and Mr Danladi Chiya for FCT South Federal Constituency, both under the APC platform.
The minister urged other states to emulate the FCT’s cross-party collaboration model, saying political alignment should serve the electorate’s interests rather than personal or partisan ambitions.
Political stakeholders, traditional leaders and women’s groups in Kuje Area Council declared support for Wike’s Rainbow Coalition initiative and its stated objective of supporting Tinubu and APC candidates.
The Chairman of Kuje Area Council, Mr Samuel Shekolo, commended Wike for promoting political stability and directing developmental attention towards the area council.
Shekolo highlighted the appointment of a Kuje indigene as Mandate Secretary for Agriculture and Rural Development, attributing his emergence as council chairman to the backing of FCT leadership.
“We have different groups here today, senior politicians, market women, cabinet women and our revered traditional rulers here.
“We all gathered to align with Wike’s direction ahead of the upcoming elections and to appreciate what this administration has done for Kuje and the entire FCT,” he said.
Speaking on behalf of traditional rulers, the District Head of Agwe, Alhaji Shuaibu Agwe, said political dynamics in the area council had shifted in favour of the Rainbow Coalition.
Agwe expressed confidence in the coalition, citing road projects and political cooperation as factors he believed would influence the forthcoming elections.
“In past elections, our hearts would be beating, and we used to go around begging people to keep the peace.
“But this time, with the Rainbow Coalition and the roads constructed from the airport to Tipper Garage and Gwagwalada, the election is going to be delivered to Tinubu,” he said.
The APC Women Leader in Kuje, Mrs Aishatu Yakubu, assured the minister that women remained important to election mobilisation and were aligned with the Rainbow Coalition.
Yakubu described the establishment of the first Women Affairs Mandate Secretariat in the FCT as a “historic gesture” demonstrating the administration’s commitment to gender inclusion.
She also said she stepped down during the council primary elections to promote party unity and stability, while appealing for political appointments and opportunities for former aspirants.
“We have seen, felt, and touched the dividends of this administration. We are ready to work, but we plead that space be created for women and former aspirants who stepped down for unity,” she said.(NAN)

items.title: Tchad : à Pala, une mission de contrôle met en lumière de graves manquements sanitaires

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : à Pala, une mission de contrôle met en lumière de graves manquements sanitaires
original_payload.original_body:
Tchad
Tchad : à Pala, une mission de contrôle met en lumière de graves manquements sanitaires
Une mission conjointe menée à Pala a révélé de graves manquements sanitaires et environnementaux dans plusieurs unités de production, annonçant des sanctions imminentes pour les récalcitrants.
Alwihda Info
07 oct. 2026
Par Djonre Nentouing Ben-Casimir
Une mission conjointe conduite par le maire de la ville de Pala, le Dr Armi Jonas, et le délégué de l’Environnement, de la Pêche et du Développement durable, Fawa Gatien Ngarga, a effectué, mardi 6 octobre, une tournée d’inspection auprès de plusieurs unités de production locales.
Ciblant prioritairement les fabricants d’eau en sachets et de glace, les unités d’extraction d’huile d’arachide ainsi que les boulangeries, l'opération visait à vérifier le strict respect des normes environnementales, sanitaires et d’hygiène.
Sur le terrain, les autorités ont relevé des insuffisances alarmantes, en particulier dans certaines structures de production d’eau et de glace. La mission fait état de conditions d'insalubrité notoires : équipements de congélation rouillés, eau d’aspect douteux, installations précaires, sachets stockés à même le sol et machines nécessitant une maintenance urgente.
Des défaillances similaires ont été constatées dans plusieurs boulangeries. Dans les unités d’extraction d’huile d’arachide, la situation s'est révélée tout aussi préoccupante, marquée par la présence de matières premières altérées, d’impuretés mélangées aux arachides et de conditions de travail bafouant les règles élémentaires d’hygiène.
Au terme de ces contrôles, le matériel non conforme a été saisi et les responsables d'une unité d'extraction ont été interpellés pour les besoins de la procédure.
Selon les autorités, cette première démarche se veut avant tout pédagogique, offrant un délai de mise en conformité aux opérateurs. Une phase répressive débutera toutefois rapidement, avec la menace de fermetures administratives pour les établissements réfractaires.
Insistant sur l’importance de la régularité administrative, le maire Dr Armi Jonas a rappelé que plusieurs entreprises exerçaient sans l’autorisation municipale requise, justifiant ainsi la nécessité de contrôles accrus.
À travers cette initiative, les services municipaux et étatiques entendent sanctuariser la protection de la santé des consommateurs et améliorer durablement le cadre de vie à Pala.

items.title: UCL: Osimhen scores as Galatasaray beat Lille 4-2

original_payload.original_title: UCL: Osimhen scores as Galatasaray beat Lille 4-2
original_payload.original_body:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen was on target as Galatasaray defeated Lille 4-2 to secure their first three points of the 2026 UEFA Champions League campaign.
The Nigerian forward sealed the victory with a goal in the 61st minute, registering his first strike in the Champions League this season and his seventh goal in all competitions for the Turkish giants.
Galatasaray took an early lead through Yunus Akgun, who found the back of the net in the second minute to give the home side a perfect start.
However, Lille fought back, with Aleksey Batrakov restoring parity in the 44th minute for the visitors.
The visitors also enjoyed an impressive first-half performance from 19-year-old Soriba Diaoune, who scored twice in the seventh and 39th minutes to complete a brace and put Galatasaray under pressure.

items.title: Opinion| Why South Sudan’s absence from the Lamu refinery project is a missed opportunity

original_payload.original_title: Opinion| Why South Sudan’s absence from the Lamu refinery project is a missed opportunity
original_payload.original_body:
As regional infrastructure developments take center stage in East Africa, a monumental energy project is unfolding on the Kenyan coast. Following the recent groundbreaking for the massive Dangote oil refinery in Lamu, designed to process a staggering 700,000 barrels of crude oil per day, the region is witnessing the largest refining facility of its kind. For South Sudan, the undisputed economic heavyweight in crude oil production within interior Africa, this development should have triggered immediate, aggressive diplomatic and economic engagement. Instead, Juba remained conspicuously absent from the foundational negotiations.
To understand the gravity of this missed opportunity, one must look back at the grand design of the Lamu Port-South Sudan-Ethiopia Transport (LAPSSET) corridor. Conceived as a multi-nation infrastructure blueprint, LAPSSET was intended to open up the landlocked interior of East Africa, integrating South Sudan, Ethiopia, Uganda, and Rwanda into a vibrant trade highway linked to the Indian Ocean. The entire logic of routing such a trade corridor through Lamu Port relied fundamentally on South Sudan’s vast oil reserves serving as the primary anchor. Yet, while neighboring governments and private capital actively shape equity stakes, Juba operated from the sidelines.
In international political economy, a brutal axiom dictates state survival: “If you are not at the table, you are on the menu.” South Sudan produces the oil that could power regional energy dynamics, yet it consistently fails to leverage its production weight into structural bargaining power. When a multi-billion-dollar infrastructure project of this magnitude is planned and constructed without early-stage equity negotiations with Juba, the writing is already on the wall. South Sudan risks becoming a captive consumer of refined products processed from its own raw resources or, worse, being squeezed out of favorable pricing. Once the project is completed, negotiating leverage disappears because you cannot renegotiate to be part of the structure once the architecture is locked in.
This passive posture exposes a lack of strategic foresight within South Sudan’s leadership. Governance has become overly reactive, lurching from crisis to crisis while missing macroeconomic shifts happening right at our borders. Through vibrant diplomacy and proactive economic planning, Juba should have secured three critical pillars at the earliest stages of negotiation. Firstly, South Sudan should have negotiated a dedicated crude pipeline running directly from Block 5B to Lamu. This would not disrupt existing export routes through Port Sudan; instead, it would give South Sudan a powerful dual-outlet posture by partnering with private capital and inviting investors such as Dangote himself to fund and build the pipeline technology, to be repaid through future crude allocations.
Secondly, a fully integrated refinery backed by a secure South Sudanese pipeline would have unlocked massive multilateral financing. With guaranteed crude feedstock, international financial institutions such as the World Bank would find it commercially viable to fund complementary road, rail, and fiber-optic networks cutting through northern Kenya and into South Sudan, bringing long-term economic stability and security to historically volatile border communities.
Thirdly, early-stage negotiations would have given Juba the chance to acquire strategic land and equity stakes directly at the Port of Lamu. Land ownership at the port terminal creates skilled industrial jobs for South Sudanese youth, while technically slashing transit costs for our imports compared to the expensive, congested logistics chains currently relying solely on Mombasa or Port Sudan.
Conclusion
The Lamu refinery project serves as a sharp wake-up call for Juba. South Sudan cannot continue to sit back as a mere provider of raw extraction while regional partners dictate the terms of value addition and distribution. If the leadership of our country continues to ignore strategic economic planning, the unfulfilled promises of governance in our country will extend far beyond domestic policy and end up crippling our external economic future. To avoid being cheated by systems built on our own resources, our government should shed its reactive shell and realize that, in the ruthless arena of regional trade, silence and absence are a guarantee of exploitation. It is time to pay keen attention to our national interest.
The writer, Michael Thon Mangok, is a political analyst based in Juba and a former host of the Wake-Up Juba political talk show at Radio Bakhita.

items.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya

original_payload.original_title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
original_payload.original_body:
Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
Image source,  Reuters
Image caption,    Travellers are subject to temperature checks at Kenyan border crossing-points
By   Patrick Jackson      and    Timothy Obiezu   ,  West Africa producer
Published
24 October 2026, 01:05 BST
Updated 3 hours ago
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.
A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.
Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.
All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said.
More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.
Kenya's latest victim had been under quarantine when she developed symptoms on 13 October, the health ministry said.
The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later.
Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner.
The US has warned its citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert.
Ebola is a  rare but deadly disease ,  external   caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.
The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
The Bundibugyo species of Ebola is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.
With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according to the International Rescue Committee, which has been working alongside both governments to contain the spread.
Kenya has introduced enhanced screening for travellers arriving from DR Congo and nine other countries it considers to be at high risk: Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic.
Travellers arriving from those countries are required to complete a digital surveillance form before boarding their flights and present a QR code to port health officials on arrival.
Kenya also ordered enhanced public health screening of aircraft arriving from those countries, as authorities seek to prevent further imported cases.
Within the country, the government has been sharing public messages to create awareness about Ebola, including encouraging people to promptly report any suspected cases and seek care at a hospital.
Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
Published
3 days ago

Published
1 day ago

Published
18 June
Nigeria's health minister said its sole confirmed case of Ebola appeared to be genetically related to a strain identified earlier in Kenya.
Prof Ali Pate said there was no evidence so far that the Kenyan patient had travelled to Nigeria, but that further testing was under way.
Health officials have been investigating whether Nigeria's first case crossed paths with Kenya's first patient. Both are believed to have travelled through Uganda's Entebbe airport earlier this month.
Uganda's health ministry announced on Friday that people who had travelled to DR Congo would no longer be able to transit via Uganda as part of its prevention measures.

items.title: PR visita Rússia e vai encontrar-se com Putin

original_payload.original_title: PR visita Rússia e vai encontrar-se com Putin
original_payload.original_body:
O chefe do Estado moçambicano, Daniel Chapo, realiza de 27 a 29 de outubro uma visita de trabalho à Rússia, com agenda para se encontrar com Vladimir Putin e participar da 3.ª Cimeira Rússia-África.
Em comunicado, a Presidência moçambicana indica que Daniel Chapo visita aquele país europeu em resposta ao convite formulado pelo seu homólogo Vladimir Putin para participar da 3.ª Cimeira Rússia-África.
Esta será a primeira participação do Presidente Daniel Chapo na Cimeira Rússia-África, uma plataforma de diálogo destinada a promover e aprofundar mecanismos e estratégias de cooperação entre a Federação da Rússia e os países africanos, conforme informação divulgada pela Presidência.
Segundo o documento, durante a cimeira, os chefes de Estado deverão adotar três documentos, nomeadamente, a declaração da 3.ª Cimeira Rússia-África, o Plano de Ação 2027-2029 e a Declaração sobre a Cooperação no Domínio do Uso Pacífico das Tecnologias de Inteligência Artificial.
“À margem do encontro, o Presidente da República manterá um encontro com o Presidente Vladimir Putin, além de interagir com a comunidade moçambicana residente na Federação da Rússia e representantes de grandes empresas russas”, lê-se no comunicado.
O chefe do Estado visita Rússia após, em julho, o ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros russo, Sergei Lavrov, avançar, em Maputo, que a Rússia está disponível para ajudar Moçambique a “eliminar” o terrorismo em Cabo Delgado.

items.title: Nigeria’s crude production rises to 1.821m bpd reflecting improved upstream activities – FG

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria’s crude production rises to 1.821m bpd reflecting improved upstream activities – FG
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Nigeria’s crude production rises to 1.821m bpd reflecting improved upstream activities – FG
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   3 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Emmanuella Anokam
Sen. Heineken Lokpobiri, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), says Nigeria’s crude oil production has risen to 1.821 million barrels per day (bpd), reflecting improved regulations and upstream activities.
Lokpobiri said this on Tuesday in Abuja at the fifth anniversary commemoration of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), established under the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA 2021).
The event was with the theme, “From Uncertainty to Stability: Unlocking the Next Phase of Investment”.
He said the increase was driven by improved collaboration between the commission, government and industry stakeholders, as well as efforts to remove bottlenecks that had slowed investment.
The minister said the government had challenged the commission to measure its performance, not by the number of regulations introduced, but by the businesses and investments it enabled.
According to him, the approach has helped to improve the operating environment and accelerate activities across the upstream sector.
“Today, we are doing 1.821 million barrels per day.
“The country has recorded more than 80 per cent success in its efforts to improve production,” he said.
Lokpobiri also highlighted the increase in drilling activities, saying the number of active rigs had risen from fewer than 10 when the administration assumed office to more than 70 currently.
He said sustained drilling activities were critical to increasing production and achieving Nigeria’s target of raising crude output to about three million bpd.
The minister said Nigeria’s vast petroleum reserves would only translate into economic value if the government continued to create an enabling environment for investment and issued licences to investors with the requisite financial and technical capacity.
He urged NUPRC to sustain its reforms and provide efficient regulatory services that would support continued growth in the upstream sector.
He said the country must provide investors with a predictable operating environment to enable it to take advantage of emerging opportunities in the global oil market.
The minister said the government remained committed to unlocking Nigeria’s petroleum resources for the benefit of Nigerians and the global energy market.
The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Dr Ekperikpe Ekpo, said regulatory stability in Nigeria’s petroleum sector must translate into increased investment, faster project delivery and greater economic value.
Expo, represented by Mrs Patience Oyekunle, Permanent Secretary of the ministry, said PIA 2021 had provided a stronger institutional and regulatory foundation for the industry by improving governance structures, transparency and regulatory processes.
He said that the next phase required industry stakeholders to move beyond reforms to measurable results.
“Regulatory stability is not an end in itself. It must translate into increased investments, accelerated projects, higher production, greater value creation and improved economic benefit for Nigerians.
“The development is, particularly, important for the gas sector, given Nigeria’s vast natural gas resources and their potential to support industrialisation, power generation, domestic energy security and regional economic development.
“Reliable gas supply begins with a healthy upstream investment environment, making regulatory efficiency critical to the development of commercially viable gas projects,” he said.
Ekpo urged NUPRC to continue strengthening regulatory stability, facilitating timely approvals, improving transparency and supporting the development of commercially valuable gas projects.
Also speaking, Mr Bayo Ojulari, Group Chief Executive Officer, Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd.), said effective regulation went beyond oversight to enabling businesses, facilitating investments and creating sustainable value.
Ojulari said NUPRC’s improved engagement with operators, clearer regulatory processes and collaborative problem-solving had created an environment where businesses could focus on delivering value.
He said NNPC Ltd. was recording progress in increasing oil and gas production, reducing costs, strengthening partnerships and attracting new investment opportunities.
According to him, the industry’s priorities include growing reserves, increasing production, accelerating gas development, commercialising undeveloped resources and strengthening Nigeria’s competitiveness in the global energy market.
Sen. Magnus Abe, Chairman, NUPRC Governing Board, said the commission had made significant progress in strengthening regulatory processes and creating a more transparent and investment-friendly upstream environment.
Abe said the new spirit of teamwork, commitment and collaboration among government institutions, regulators and industry stakeholders had helped unlock opportunities across the petroleum sector.
He said the commission’s priorities must include increasing upstream production, attracting investment, unlocking marginal and stranded resources, reducing regulatory bottlenecks and ensuring responsible management of Nigeria’s natural resources.( NAN )

items.title: Cameroun : le gouvernement appuie le programme « Cacao Bio 1000 » pour booster la filière

original_payload.original_title: Cameroun : le gouvernement appuie le programme « Cacao Bio 1000 » pour booster la filière
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Cameroun : le gouvernement appuie le programme « Cacao Bio 1000 » pour booster la filière
Le gouvernement camerounais soutient le programme « Cacao Bio 1000 », visant à associer production biologique, commerce équitable et meilleure rémunération des producteurs locaux sur les marchés internationaux.
Alwihda Info
21 oct. 2026
© DR
Par Abraham Ndjana Modo
Le Cameroun entend conforter la place de son cacao sur les marchés internationaux en misant sur la qualité, la traçabilité, la durabilité et une meilleure valorisation de sa production. Cette ambition était au cœur de la signature, ce lundi 19 octobre 2026, d'une convention de partenariat entre la coopérative Unité Moderne de Production de Cacao d’Excellence (UMO.PRO.CAO.E.SCOOPS) d’Ayos, représentée par le président de son Conseil exécutif, Mveng Ateba Sébastien, et la société Protect First AG, basée au Liechtenstein et représentée par son PDG, Ralf Van Deest.
Présidée par le ministre du Commerce, Luc Magloire Mbarga Atangana, cette cérémonie s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme « Cacao Bio 1000 », qui vise à promouvoir un cacao camerounais répondant aux exigences croissantes des marchés internationaux. Au-delà de la formalisation d'un accord entre deux entités, l'enjeu est de bâtir une vision commune sur le long terme associant les producteurs, la coopérative, Protect First AG et les clients internationaux.
Le choix de la coopérative d’Ayos ne doit rien au hasard. Elle figure parmi les acteurs reconnus pour leur engagement, comme l'atteste sa médaille de bronze obtenue lors d'un concours international à Amsterdam. De son côté, Protect First AG mise sur un modèle reposant sur deux piliers : la production biologique sans intrants chimiques et la commercialisation sous le label du commerce équitable (Fair Trade).
Pour le ministre du Commerce, cette initiative s'inscrit en droite ligne des orientations gouvernementales visant à améliorer la rémunération des producteurs. En apportant sa caution à ce partenariat, le gouvernement espère qu'il servira de modèle pour l'ensemble de la filière. L'ambition des pouvoirs publics est de faire du cacao camerounais une référence mondiale, avec des prix pouvant atteindre le double de ceux pratiqués dans d'autres grands pays producteurs. « Le cacao du Cameroun reste au sommet du monde », a conclu Luc Magloire Mbarga Atangana.

items.title: Cash-strapped China targets offshore wealth with new tax

original_payload.original_title: Cash-strapped China targets offshore wealth with new tax
original_payload.original_body:
China is aiming to claw back some of the colossal riches kept overseas by the country’s millionaires and billionaires, who have until Thursday to pay new taxes levied by Beijing aimed at filling a growing fiscal hole.
The rapid rise of China’s economy in recent decades has produced legions of super-rich — many of  who keep their fortunes in trusts across Hong Kong, Singapore, Tokyo and other locations.
However, regulations announced in July levy a tax of 20 per cent on dividends and interest gained from offshore trusts, with a 90-day “transition period” for initial payments concluding on Thursday.
The law has prompted a flurry of activity in recent weeks for China’s wealthiest individuals and families to sort out their financial affairs, analysts say.

En marge de la huitième réunion de coordination de l’Union africaine, le ministre d’État, ministre des Affaires étrangères, de l’Intégration africaine et des Tchadiens de l’étranger, Ahmed Kogri, a rencontré son homologue égyptien, Dr Badr Abdelatty, à Al-Alamein. Au cours des échanges, les deux parties ont salué la qualité des relations entre N’Djamena et Le Caire et réaffirmé leur volonté de consolider la coopération entre les deux pays. Les discussions ont également permis d’aborder les évolutions de la situation au Sahel et dans les pays limitrophes, dans un contexte régional marqué par des enjeux sécuritaires et politiques importants.

items.title: Afrique centrale : le trafic de médicaments, une menace majeure pour la santé publique selon l’ONU

original_payload.original_title: Afrique centrale : le trafic de médicaments, une menace majeure pour la santé publique selon l’ONU
original_payload.original_body:
Le trafic de médicaments en Afrique centrale, alimenté par des difficultés d'accès aux soins, constitue une "menace majeure pour la santé publique", selon un rapport de l'Office des Nations unies contre la drogue et le crime (ONUDC) publié mardi 6 octobre 2026.
Dans les six pays de la Communauté économique et monétaire d'Afrique centrale (CEMAC), qui  "présentent des indicateurs de santé parmi les plus défavorables au monde",  l'écart entre les besoins en santé et l'accès effectif à des produits sûrs et abordables "favorisent le développement d'un marché illicite", alerte le rapport co-signé avec l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) et la CEMAC.
Le trafic, qui  "constitue une menace majeure pour la santé publique"  dans la région selon l'ONUDC, concerne des médicaments falsifiés, de qualité inférieure ou non approuvés par les autorités, mais aussi des produits détournés des circuits officiels. Les antibiotiques, antipaludéens, antidouleurs, anti-inflammatoires, ou psychoactifs comme le tramadol et la prégabaline figurent parmi les produits concernés.
Au moins 251 tonnes de médicaments ont été saisies entre le Cameroun, le Gabon, le Tchad, le Congo, la Guinée équatoriale et la Centrafrique entre 2020 et 2025, selon ce rapport. Et ces dernières années, ce trafic a fait l'objet d'une "intensification et d'une diversification", a alerté un responsable de l'ONUDC lors d'une conférence de presse mardi.
Ce commerce illégale favorise  « des échecs thérapeutiques, des intoxications et des décès évitables »  et contribue au développement de résistances aux antimicrobiens. Et les produits issus de ce trafic se retrouvent parfois "dans des structures autorisées, généralement perçues comme sûres par les patients", dénoncent le rapport.
À l'échelle de l'Afrique subsaharienne, l'OMS estime en 2017 que la consommation de ces médicaments frauduleux pouvait être associée à des centaines de milliers de décès chaque année. Les produits arrivent notamment par les ports de la région, avant d'emprunter les grands axes routiers, favorisés par la porosité des frontières, et passent aussi par voie aérienne, dans le fret ou les bagages de passagers.
Ce trafic implique notamment des groupes armés, présents dans certaines régions du Cameroun, du Tchad ou de la Centrafrique, à travers le pillage de centres de santé, la revente de produits ou le prélèvement de « taxes » sur les convois. En plus "d'alimenter la criminalité organisée et d'affaiblir les institutions publiques", il favorise l'usage non médical des produits associés aux phénomènes de dépendance, insiste le rapport, qui appelle à "renforcer la coopération internationale" pour endiguer le phénomène.

items.title: Dangote Cement commits millions in scholarship scheme

original_payload.original_title: Dangote Cement commits millions in scholarship scheme
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Dangote Cement commits millions in scholarship scheme
By  Ismail Abdulaziz   ·   2 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
Dangote Cement Plc, Gboko Plant has awarded multi-million-Naira scholarships to tertiary and secondary school students from its six host communities in Benue.
The company also presented starter packs, working tools and certificates to graduates of its Youth Empowerment Programme to enable them to establish their own businesses, apply the skills acquired during the training and become financially reliant.
The Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, lauded Dangote Cement Plc for its community development interventions, calling on other private sector players to adopt similar initiatives to promote socio-economic development in their host communities.
Alake, who was represented by the Federal Mines Officer of the Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development in Benue, Achi Gregory, urged the company to sustain its commitment to implementing community development programmes agreed upon with its host communities.
Speaking at the official presentation ceremony, Group Head, Social Performance, Dangote Cement Plc, Mr Wakeel Olayiwola, said the implementation of the Community Development Agreement underscores Dangote Cement’s commitment to equipping youths with practical skills and resources.
He said this would promote entrepreneurship, create employment opportunities and improve livelihoods in its host communities.
Olayiwola, who was represented by the Head of Social Performance of the Dangote Cement, Gboko Plant, Dr Johnson Kor, said the scholarship and youth empowerment programmes came against the backdrop of several other programmes recently executed by the company.
He said that others programmes include the farmers and women empowerment programmes.
The Acting Plant Director, Dangote Cement, Gboko, Arbind Singh, said: “This annual scholarship scheme for indigent students of the host communities is an indication of our company’s commitment to its Corporate Social Responsibilities (CSR).”
Singh, who was represented by the company’s General Manager, Production, Tabershima Soom, said: “The Gboko Plant has already launched 150 Women Empowerment Programme and 50 Farmerss Empowerment Programme where women were provided with cash to support their businesses, and farmers were supported with farm inputs.”
The beneficiary communities for these programmes are: Tse-Kucha, Quarry, Amua, Mbazembe, Mbatur, and Pass Brothers.
Speaking on behalf of the Benue State Attorney-General, the Chairman of the Mineral Resources and Environmental Management Committee (MIREMCO), Dooshima Orosaga, commended Dangote Cement Plc for its compliance with the Community Development Agreement (CDA).
She urged the beneficiaries and host communities to maximise the benefits of the company’s interventions.
Chairman of the Gboko Local Government, Yina Elias, said the state government would continue to provide the support needed for the company to succeed, adding that the Dangote Cement Plc is an exemplary company in Corporate Social Responsibilities programmes.
In his remarks, the District Head of Ukpekpe, Chief Tsegba Igbarumun, commended Dangote Cement Plc’s Gboko Plant for its contributions to the community, assuring the company of the community’s continued support.
He said the community valued its mutually beneficial relationship with the company and would continue to serve as its ambassadors.
A beneficiary of the Youth Empowerment Programme, Mr Ignatius Aondohemba, expressed appreciation to Dangote Cement Plc for the support, pledging to put the skills and resources provided to good use and build a business that would enable him to become an employer of labour.(NAN)

Une vidéo de surveillance diffusée lundi 19 octobre devant la Haute Cour de Durban montre un homme ressemblant à l’un des sept accusés suivre le rappeur sud-africain Kiernan « AKA » Forbes à l’aéroport international King Shaka, avant son assassinat en février 2023.
L’analyste en vidéosurveillance Sandile Khuzwayo a présenté des images retraçant l’arrivée d’AKA à Durban et son passage vers une agence de location de voitures. Un homme apparaît derrière lui puis à proximité de l’entrée, selon les comptes rendus concordants de TimesLIVE, EWN et eNCA.
L’accusation n’a toutefois pas demandé au témoin d’identifier formellement cet homme à l’audience. Lors de précédentes procédures de libération sous caution, le ministère public avait associé cette séquence à Mziwethemba Harvey Gwabeni, le quatrième accusé. Cette identification reste contestée dans le procès en cours.
L’avocat de la défense William Nicholson a soutenu que le témoin ne pouvait pas déterminer l’identité de la personne filmée. Il a également interrogé les conditions dans lesquelles les images avaient été transmises aux enquêteurs et présentées au tribunal.
Les sept prévenus sont jugés pour les meurtres d’AKA et du chef cuisinier Tebello « Tibz » Motsoane, tués par balle devant le restaurant Wish, sur Florida Road à Durban, en février 2023. Tous ont plaidé non coupables.
Le témoignage de Sandile Khuzwayo doit se poursuivre mardi 20 octobre. La procédure se poursuit et les accusés restent présumés innocents tant qu’une culpabilité n’a pas été établie.

FNE 2026 au Tchad : la coordination s'organise pour la réussite du Forum national sur l'emploi
À l'approche du FNE 2026, la Coordination du comité d'organisation a tenu une réunion stratégique à l'ONAPE pour structurer les commissions et lancer les plans d'action.

Dans le cadre des préparatifs de la deuxième édition du Forum national sur l'emploi (FNE 2026), la Coordination du comité d'organisation a tenu, ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, une réunion de travail présidée par M.
